articles.title: Astronomers just named an asteroid after 'Weird Al' Yankovic
articles.summary: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) recently approved naming an asteroid after musician and actor 'Weird' Al Yankovic.
articles.body:
"Weird Al" Yankovic's name has been approved for an asteroid that was discovered in 1981 and resides in the main belt of asteroids between Mars and Jupiter.

The asteroid, formally known as (14331) Alyankovic, joins other musical-themed celebrity monikers on asteroids, such as Elvis, Freddiemercury, Aretha, Dollyparton, and all members of the Beatles.

Living persons can have their names attached to asteroids and other "small bodies," but the process can take years and must meet a multi-page set of requirements as well as the muster of the International Astronomical Union's working group that names small bodies.

It may not be a slime creature from outer space, but you can finally find "Weird Al" Yankovic's name flying beyond our planet.

The American musician and comedian's name was recently approved for an asteroid , or space rock, that zooms around our solar system about once every four years.

The asteroid is formally known as (14331) Alyankovic , or 1981 EC26. 1981 refers to the year of the asteroid's discovery, and Yankovic's name for it was approved by the International Astronomical Union (IAU), the official body that arbitrates the monikers of things in the universe .

Planetary scientist Allison McGraw, an alumna of the University of Arizona who is now with the Lunar and Planetary Science Institute, backed the nomination with several other planetary science researchers, according to the Tucson Star . On Sunday (Sept. 20), McGraw presented Yankovic backstage with a plaque commemorating the naming of the asteroid, ahead of Yankovic's performance at the Tucson Arena.

"I've been working on not being starstruck, the same way I am every time I meet astronauts," McGraw said in the Tucson Star's report, ahead of the meeting. "I'm gonna do my best not to be starstruck, or I guess 'rock struck', but I have the feeling that he's going to be really cool."

Alyankovic (the asteroid) was discovered in 1981 and resides in the main belt of asteroids found between Mars and Jupiter . It is visible from Earth , but only in a good telescope as its absolute magnitude is 16; for comparison, the faintest stars visible to the naked eye are roughly magnitude 5 or 6, under dark-sky conditions.

Alyankovic joins several other musical-themed celebrity monikers on asteroids, such as 17059 Elvis, 17473 Freddiemercury, 249516 Aretha (after Aretha Franklin), 10731 Dollyparton, and all members of the Beatles (both individually, and as a group for 8749 Beatles.)

Meanwhile, Al Yankovic (the singer) has been belting out funny space-related tunes for decades, including the rap-like "Sir Isaac Newton vs. Bill Nye", an Obi-Wan Kenobi-centered retelling of Star Wars: The Phantom Menace called "The Saga Begins," and the self-explanatory and classic "Attack of the Radioactive Hamsters from a Planet Near Mars."

While living persons can have their names attached to asteroids and other "small bodies" like comets, the process can take years, and any name must meet a multi-page set of requirements as well as the muster of the IAU's working group that names small bodies.

"Names have traditionally been assigned to many small bodies and have drawn from mythological characters, planetary scientists, astronomers, and accomplished scientists, engineers, and technicians in other fields. People who have made contributions to the arts, sports, medicine, and other aspects of society are also recognized. Discoverers have also used names of personal significance to them," the IAU states.

Some of the other institutions or things named in the Sept. 9 IAU notice include:

(15708) Metsoc = 1988 RB12. It is named for the Meteoritical Society, which has an annual conference and hosts the Meteoritics and Planetary Science journal, in large part to showcase countries that are not as widely represented.

(20176) Aliciagoyena = 1996 XK29. This is named after Alicia Goyena, an educator and history teacher in Uruguay who was director of the women's section of the Instituto Batlle y Ordóñez in Montevideo.

(31550) Beckmaier = 1999 DT7. Beck Maier is a telescope operator at the Lowell Observatory's Lowell Discovery Telescope in Arizona.

(50271) Albertoanunziato = 2000 CW. Alberto Anunziato is an Argentinian amateur astronomer whose work includes founding the Argentine Lunar Society, being secretary of the Ibero-American Astronomy League, and teaching at the Autonomous University of Entre Ríos.

(74025) Marquette = 1998 HA6. Jean-Baptiste Marquette is a retired French astrophysicist known for mapping the chemistry of interstellar clouds.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Bob Dylan: 'People seldom do what they believe in. They do what is convenient, then repent,' a powerful life lesson about the gap between values and actions
articles.summary: Explore Bob Dylan's insightful quote on the conflict between beliefs and actions, delving into its relevance in our lives today and the powerful message of regret over convenience.
articles.body: Knowing what we believe is one thing; actually sticking to it can be much harder when the situation gets uncomfortable. That tension is at the heart of a line Dylan wrote in 'Brownsville Girl'. Even though the song came out decades ago, the idea behind those words still feels surprisingly familiar in everyday life.Today’s quote of the day by Bob Dylan reads: “People seldom do what they believe in. They do what is convenient, then repent.”What does Bob Dylan's quote mean?Dylan's words point to a contradiction that can show up in ordinary life. We often know exactly where we stand until a situation actually puts those beliefs to the test. When there is an easy way out, following what we believe in can suddenly feel much harder.People do not always go against their own values knowingly. There are moments when stress, emotions or the pressure of everyday life can influence a decision before we have much time to think about it. At times, choosing the simpler option may seem like the most practical thing to do, whether it saves us from an uncomfortable conversation, prevents an argument or simply helps us deal with something quickly. Later, though, we may realise that the choice we made was not quite in line with what we normally believe. Later, they may look back and wish they had handled the situation differently.The word “repent” gives the quote its strongest emotional note. It brings in the idea of regret after realising that our actions did not quite reflect what we believed. Rather than simply criticising human behaviour, Dylan seems to point toward a conflict that many people have faced at some point in their lives.The line appears in 'Brownsville Girl', a song written by Dylan with playwright Sam Shepard. The official Bob Dylan website credits both writers and lists the song as part of 'Knocked Out Loaded', released in 1986.Why is Bob Dylan's quote relevant today?We can be completely sure about what we believe, but making the right choice becomes harder when we are actually put on the spot. A stressful day, fear of the consequences, not having enough time or simply wanting to avoid an argument can all push us toward a different decision.For instance, a person might notice something unfair but stay quiet because they do not want to become part of the situation. Someone else might genuinely want to spend more time with their family but repeatedly find work, deadlines and other responsibilities getting in the way. Neither decision may seem significant on its own, yet both show the gap that can sometimes appear between what we intend to do and what we actually do.Perhaps that is the reason Dylan's words still hit home. We have all had moments when we knew what we believed, yet ended up doing something else. It does not always mean we were being dishonest with ourselves. Sometimes a situation simply gets complicated, and in the moment, we choose whatever seems easiest to deal with.Bob Dylan's early lifeLong before Bob Dylan became one of the most talked-about names in music, he was a young boy growing up in Minnesota with a growing interest in songs and performers. Born in Duluth on May 24, 1941, Dylan spent much of his childhood in Hibbing.He came to New York in 1961 and became a part of the local folk scene by performing wherever he could and getting to know other musicians. The small clubs gave him the freedom to try out new songs in front of audiences. It was a modest beginning, but Dylan's songwriting was starting to get noticed.Then the 1960s changed the scale of his career. America was going through a period of major social and cultural change and Dylan's songs found a natural place in that conversation. 'Blowin' in the Wind' and 'The Times They Are a-Changin'' travelled well beyond the folk clubs where he had first performed.How did Bob Dylan rise to fame?His decision to perform with an electric guitar at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival became one of the moments most closely associated with that change, drawing plenty of attention at the time.His songwriting continued to evolve through albums including 'Highway 61 Revisited', 'Blonde on Blonde' and 'Blood on the Tracks'. His creative interests were not limited to music either. Over the years, he also worked with poetry, prose and visual art.His influence on literature received another major recognition in 2016, when Dylan was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for creating new poetic expressions within the American song tradition.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Koppal Gavi Mutt Pontiff to inaugurate Dasara 2026
articles.summary: Koppal Gavi Mutt pontiff Sri Abhinava Gavishiddheshwar Mahaswami will inaugurate Mysuru Dasara 2026 on Oct 11; festival ends Oct 21.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Koppal Gavi Mutt pontiff, who’s won accolades as water-conservation warrior and social-welfare sage, will inaugurate the 2026 edition of 10-day Mysuru Dasara festivities starting on Oct 11.Chief minister DK Shivakumar informed the legislative assembly Thursday Abhinava Gavishiddheshwar Mahaswami, 49, has accepted the govt’s invitation. He said, “I spoke to the seer on Thursday morning and requested him to declare the state festival open.”The choice brings a prominent spiritual and social figure from North Karnataka to the centre of the state’s biggest cultural celebration. The Dasara concludes on Oct 21 with a grand Vijayadashami parade.Abhinava Gavishiddheshwar Mahaswami is the 18th pontiff and assumed charge in 2002. His ‘Jala Deekshe’ campaign in North Karnataka focused on reviving and desilting lakes and addressing severe water scarcity. Under his leadership, the mutt has continued its work in education, food and spiritual service, including providing free boarding and educational support to students from rural and economically disadvantaged backgrounds.Koppal Gavi Mutt is known for the annual Gavisiddheshwara Jatre, popularly called ‘Ajjana Jatre’, one of the region’s largest religious gatherings. The mutt has traditionally used the occasion to recognise achievers from different walks of life.The selection of the seer for Mysuru Dasara comes after several names were discussed for the prestigious inauguration. articles.title: Spurs legend Gregg Popovich marries former assistant coach's ex-wife
articles.summary: Gregg Popovich married Mary Barth Budenholzer on Sept. 16, according to Bexar County records. The legendary coach's new wife was previously married to Mike B...
articles.body:
Gregg Popovich coached the San Antonio Spurs from 1996 to 2025, winning a league-record 1,390 regular-season games, 170 postseason games and five NBA championships.

For four of those championships and quite a few of the other victories, one of Popovich's assistant coaches was his new wife's ex-husband.

Popovich, 77, married Mary Barth Budenholzer on Sept. 16, the Bexar County, Texas, clerk's office has confirmed.

Budenholzer is a 61-year-old native of Corpus Christi, according to multiple media outlets, and was once married to Mike Budenholzer , who was a Spurs assistant coach under Popovich from 1996 to 2013. He went on to become the head coach of the Atlanta Hawks, Milwaukee Bucks and Phoenix Suns, winning an NBA championship with the Bucks in 2021.

The Budenholzers are said to share four children and to have divorced in 2016.

Popovich was married to Erin Popovich for four decades until her 2018 death at age 67. They have two children and multiple grandchildren.

On Nov. 2, 2024, Popovich suffered a stroke before a game at Frost Bank Center, the Spurs' home arena. Assistant coach Mitch Johnson was named interim coach. That title became permanent on May 2, 2025, when Popovich stepped down after 29 years as San Antonio's coach.

A member of the Spurs' front office since 1994, Popovich currently serves as the team's president of basketball operations. He was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 2023.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Piano Prodigy Elias Phoenix, Who Appeared on “Ellen”, Accuses Brother and Late Mom of Physical and Emotional Abuse as Child
articles.summary: The former star, now 20, claimed his mother and brother “would mentally torture” him during his childhood
articles.body:
Elias Phoenix, a child piano prodigy who made several appearances on The Ellen DeGeneres Show , claimed that his brother and late mother physically and emotionally abused him as a kid

In a series of posts to X on Sept. 16, Elias detailed his allegations and shared videos where it appeared that his mother screamed at him and called him expletives

"genuinely a miracle I'm still alive," he wrote in one post

Elias Phoenix — a child piano prodigy — has come forward with allegations of abuse against his brother and late mother.

Phoenix, 20, first gained prominence in 2014 through a series of appearances on The Ellen DeGeneres Show , where he won over audiences with his incredible piano talents, his adorable personality and his characteristic top hat. He also performed as a child at Carnegie Hall and competed as a piano duo alongside his twin brother Zion on season 11 of America's Got Talent .

In a series of posts to X on Sept. 16, Elias claimed that his mother and brother physically and emotionally abused him on multiple occasions throughout his childhood.

In one post, Elias shared several videos from 2017 where it appeared that his mother — who has since died of cancer — screamed at him and called him expletives while he was recording an audition for The Juilliard School, a prestigious conservatory.

"as seen, zion and mom would mentally torture me, zion locked me out the house at one point, and mom is blaming me for her dying of cancer," Elias alleged in his post.

"this was not a one-time occurence either, these mfs would abuse tf outta me physically and emotionally directly before shows, especially during the later ones," he continued. "genuinely a miracle I'm still alive."

Elias went on to claim that the alleged abuse had left him with "anorexia from them both calling me fat repeatedly, constant self hate, fear of ever playing music again, and really bad suicidal ideation/depression."

"but somehow i continue to thrive, and stay surprisingly insanely Elias Phoenix thru everything, and im so thankful to still be fighting for me," he wrote. "I make beats now, made by only me, heard by only me, made for only me, and there's comfort in knowing no one is making me do it."

Elias did not share further details about how or when the alleged abuse occurred. PEOPLE has reached out to Zion for comment.

Since his stardom as a child, Elias has kept a relatively low profile online, only occasionally sharing life updates to his X account. In March 2024, he celebrated passing his final GED tests, and the next month, he marked his 18th birthday.

In August, he shared a video to YouTube — his first post to his channel in six years — of a song that he produced titled "_arewestilllive."

articles.title: Elevação do nível do mar na Califórnia destrói casas e praias | G1
articles.standfirst: El Niño intensifica ondas no Pacífico, enquanto autoridades se preparam para novos eventos extremos e possíveis impactos de marés mais altas nos próximos meses.
articles.summary: O fenômeno El Niño intensifica a elevação do nível do mar na Califórnia, provocando erosão costeira severa e a destruição de casas em regiões como Malibu e Dana Point.
articles.body:
Pequenas ondas batem contra penhasco de arenito em Encinitas, na Califórnia 16 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Mike Blake

Em Malibu, o Oceano Pacífico abriu um buraco perto da casa do astro de cinema Nicolas Cage e causou estragos em propriedades à beira-mar. Ao longo da Beach Road, na cidade de Dana Point, as ondas destruíram uma casa e obrigaram a prefeitura a desocupar ou restringir a ocupação de outras 16.

Esses danos, que se estenderam por todo o sul da Califórnia neste verão, foram provocados por uma série de ciclones e furacões do Pacífico Oriental, intensificados pelo fenômeno climático conhecido como El Niño. Embora os furacões não tenham atingido o continente na Califórnia, eles geraram ondas gigantes que se chocaram contra a costa, arrancando a areia das praias e transformando um litoral que faz parte da identidade da Califórnia tanto quanto Hollywood ou o Vale do Silício.

Especialistas afirmam que ondas ainda mais violentas podem chegar nos próximos meses, quando ciclos climáticos naturais, intensificados pelas mudanças climáticas, podem coincidir com as marés mais altas.

“Tudo indica que este será um inverno bastante épico em termos de riscos potenciais”, disse Patrick Barnard, diretor de pesquisa do Centro de Resiliência Climática Costeira da Universidade da Califórnia em Santa Cruz. “Tudo é amplificado pelas mudanças climáticas.”

A Califórnia declarou preventivamente, nesta semana, estado de emergência para ajudar a mobilizar equipes de resgate e de primeiros socorros, em preparação para mais turbulências causadas pelo El Niño, que surgiu em junho. A previsão é de que o fenômeno demonstre seus maiores efeitos até o final do ano e no início de 2027.

Na sexta-feira (25), outro furacão, o Polo, se formou na costa do Pacífico mexicano. Ele pode enviar mais ondas para o norte. As autoridades cancelaram a primeira edição do Ocean Way Festival, marcada para este fim de semana em Santa Mônica , depois que as ondas causadas pela tempestade e o escoamento das águas do furacão Marie, durante o fim de semana do Dia do Trabalho, corroeram grande parte do local do show, logo ao sul do píer.

O El Niño ocorre a cada poucos anos, quando as águas superficiais do Oceano Pacífico tropical central e oriental ficam excepcionalmente quentes, alterando a circulação atmosférica e o clima em todo o mundo.

O nível do mar no sul da Califórnia subiu de 20 cm a 30 cm ao longo do último século. Um El Niño forte poderia elevar temporariamente o nível do mar em mais 15 a 30 cm.

Relacionada ao El Niño está a onda de Kelvin subaquática, que poderia elevar temporariamente o nível do mar em mais 15 a 30 cm. A primeira grande onda de Kelvin do atual El Niño deve chegar à Califórnia no início de outubro, segundo Michael Jacox, oceanógrafo da Administração Oceânica e Atmosférica Nacional dos EUA.

Os efeitos podem coincidir com marés-reinas sazonalmente extremas que ocorrem durante a fase de amplificação das marés do ciclo nodal lunar de 18,6 anos. O El Niño também pode produzir tempestades intensas conhecidas como “rios atmosféricos”, que frequentemente inundam áreas costeiras e erodem os penhascos das praias.

O litoral da Califórnia, geralmente íngreme, até agora poupou em grande parte os moradores das inundações crônicas observadas em áreas costeiras baixas em outras partes do mundo.

Em Carlsbad, uma cidade de 112 mil habitantes a cerca de 56 km ao norte de San Diego, a areia desapareceu quase da noite para o dia da praia de Tamarack, a joia de uma cidade que arrecada 14% de seu orçamento operacional com impostos sobre quartos de hotel.

Adam Young, geomorfologista costeiro do Instituto Scripps de Oceanografia da UC San Diego, visitou Tamarack recentemente, escalando pedras onde antes havia uma praia arenosa. Logo ao sul, o oceano engoliu a praia completamente, invadindo um estacionamento que antes permitia aos visitantes estacionarem a poucos passos da areia.

Os surfistas ainda lotam Tamarack. Mas uma praia que costumava estar repleta de turistas e moradores locais agora tem apenas alguns visitantes que ocupam um pedaço da pouca areia que resta.

“Espero que consigam encontrar uma solução, porque, sinceramente, acho que a Mãe Natureza vai levar tudo de volta até que eles parem com isso, certo?”, disse o surfista Alex Stott após uma sessão matinal. “Está ficando claro que ela pode levar a praia inteira, se quiser, bem rapidamente.”

articles.title: Tiquira do Maranhão ganha selo de Indicação Geográfica | G1
articles.standfirst: Reconhecimento vale para a produção da bebida em cinco municípios. Destilado feito de mandioca tem registros de fabricação no estado desde o período colonial.
articles.summary: Reconhecimento vale para a produção da bebida em cinco municípios. Destilado feito de mandioca tem registros de fabricação no estado desde o período colonial.
articles.body:
De cor azulada, tiquira é bebida típica de São Luís — Foto: Maurício Araya / G1

A tiquira produzida no Maranhão recebeu o reconhecimento de Indicação Geográfica (IG). O registro foi concedido pelo Instituto Nacional da Propriedade Industrial (INPI) na modalidade Indicação de Procedência (IP) e publicado na terça-feira (22).

Na prática, a Indicação Geográfica identifica produtos que ficaram conhecidos por sua relação com determinado território . No caso da tiquira, o INPI reconheceu o nome geográfico “Maranhão” pela reputação histórica do estado na produção da bebida.

🍶 A certificação está relacionada à tiquira produzida em cinco municípios maranhenses :

A área foi delimitada a partir da presença da cadeia produtiva e da continuidade da fabricação tradicional da bebida nesses municípios.

O pedido de reconhecimento foi apresentado pela Cooperativa dos Produtores de Tiquira e Agricultores Familiares de Guaribas de Urbano Santos (Cooptaf Guaribas). O INPI informou que o certificado de registro será emitido eletronicamente.

O uso da Indicação de Procedência, porém, não fica restrito aos integrantes da cooperativa. Produtores estabelecidos nos cinco municípios poderão usar a identificação desde que cumpram as regras de produção e os mecanismos de controle definidos para a IG.

🌱 Para conceder o reconhecimento, o INPI levou em consideração a história e a reputação da produção da tiquira no Maranhão.

Segundo a documentação apresentada ao instituto, a produção tradicional começa com o processamento da mandioca para a elaboração de beijus. Eles passam por fermentação natural e, depois, a massa é destilada em alambiques de cobre para dar origem à bebida.

O termo tiquira tem origem na palavra tupi “tykir”, que significa “cair gota a gota”, em referência ao processo de destilação artesanal da bebida.

De acordo com a documentação analisada pelo INPI, o Maranhão concentra a produção contínua do destilado e possui registros de fabricação desde o período colonial, ligados ao desenvolvimento da atividade agrícola no estado.

O registro também estabelece regras para o modo de produção, os padrões da bebida e o controle dos produtores autorizados a utilizar a Indicação de Procedência. A proteção concedida pelo INPI é para o nome geográfico “Maranhão” associado à tiquira produzida dentro da área reconhecida.

Tiquira já é Patrimônio Cultural do Maranhão

A importância cultural da bebida já havia sido reconhecida oficialmente em 2023, quando a tiquira recebeu o título de Patrimônio Cultural de Natureza Imaterial do Maranhão .

O reconhecimento levou em consideração os saberes tradicionais envolvidos na produção artesanal da bebida, transmitidos entre gerações. O registro também prevê medidas de preservação desse conhecimento e de continuidade da produção.

Neste fim de semana, o Pátio Brasil Shopping recebe uma experiência gratuita de ginástica voltada para crianças de 5 a 12 anos. A ação realizada em parceria com a KCGA, escola de ginástica artística, convida o público a conhecer e vivenciar a modalidade por meio de aulas práticas e apresentações de ginastas.

Durante o fim de semana, professores da KCGA conduzirão aulas de 30 minutos, proporcionando aos participantes um primeiro contato com os movimentos e fundamentos da ginástica artística. A atividade busca aproximar o público infantil da prática esportiva de forma acessível.

No sábado (26) e no domingo (27), além das aulas, o público poderá acompanhar apresentações de ginastas, durante o período da tarde.

Ao longo dos dois dias, o público poderá participar de atividades físicas, práticas de autocuidado e equilíbrio, experiências de recuperação, aulas, palestras, ativações de marcas, gastronomia, música e atrações para diferentes idades e perfis.

A novidade desta edição é a Arena Cycling — uma arena de bike indoor dedicada ao universo do ciclismo, com aulas coletivas, música e experiências diversas relacionadas a movimento e performance. Além disso, o público também vai poder curtir aulas de Kangoo Jump, funcional fight, meditação, yoga, mobilidade, crossfit, áreas de massagem e relaxamento, banheira de gelo, futmesa, altinha e muito mais.

Filho de pais separados, ele deixa a casa da mãe para morar com o pai enquanto tenta reencontrar o sentido em sua vida. O texto provoca uma reflexão sobre as relações familiares e os mistérios insondáveis da mente.

Fora das histórias conhecidas, porém, eles apresentam outras personalidades e relações, criando uma narrativa que brinca com o imaginário dos contos infantis. A encenação combina música, texto, luz, figurino e humor para conduzir o público para uma história nova e cheia de personalidade.

O Magic Ice Cream transforma o universo dos sorvetes em diversão com brinquedos infláveis, piscina de bolinhas e espaços temáticos que convidam a criançada a explorar e soltar a imaginação, até 12 de outubro, Dia das Crianças.

Entre os destaques está o Candy Slide, um escorregador inflável de seis metros de altura. Depois de chegar ao topo da estrutura, as crianças encaram uma grande descida que termina em uma piscina de bolinhas.

A experiência não acaba por aí. As crianças podem aproveitar o Ice Cream Truck, espaço inspirado nos tradicionais carrinhos de sorvete com elementos cenográficos e cores vibrantes. A estrutura completa o circuito e reforça a proposta do parque de unir aventura, imaginação e brincadeira em uma mesma experiência.

O espetáculo Tribos consagra a trajetória de 32 anos da companhia paraense. A montagem aborda a cultura e os costumes dos povos indígenas, sua relação com a sociedade e temas como a defesa da identidade, a resistência e a relação com a natureza.

Os figurinos e adereços são inspirados em diferentes etnias, como kayapó, terena, munduruku e assurini. A trilha sonora utiliza sons gravados de diferentes povos, além de artistas internacionais.

A seleção reúne desenhos, pinturas a óleo e acrílica e trabalhos que se afastam da imagem mais difundida de Athos como mestre da azulejaria geométrica. Entre as surpresas está uma série dedicada ao Carnaval, ligada às memórias de infância e juventude do artista no Catete, no Rio de Janeiro.

articles.title: Karol G no Brasil: Detalhes do show que chega a São Paulo em 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Turnê 'Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour', que vem para SP em fevereiro de 2027, mescla estilos latino-americanos e reforça momento de dominação global da artista. Veja como é o show.
articles.summary: A turnê Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour traz Karol G no Brasil em fevereiro de 2027 com um espetáculo que une reggaeton e funk na Arena Pacaembu, em São Paulo.
articles.body:
De vez em quando, testemunhamos um show que marca história na carreira de um artista. Foi essa a sensação ao ver Karol G (com 53 mil pessoas presentes, em sua primeira de duas noites esgotadas), no dia 17 de setembro no MetLife Stadium, em Nova York.

O show foi da turnê "Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour", que desembarca no Brasil em fevereiro. E é um retrato da artista colombiana no auge de sua dominação global (até aqui). Abaixo, entenda o que esperar do show de Karol G:

A "Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour" é a quinta turnê de Karol e, a essa altura, ela sabe bem como construir um megashow. A apresentação é calientíssima, com megaestrutura e dividida em cinco atos. Ao longo de duas horas e meia de show, há algumas baladas e muitos, mas muitos, momentos enérgicos e sensuais.

Karol G durante show no Metlife Stadium, em Nova York, no dia 17 de setembro — Foto: Divulgação/Henry Hwu

É o tipo de espetáculo que se espera de grandes artistas pop internacionais, mas, diferente do formato de sempre, não é feito por americanos para americanos.

Ao longo do show, Karol vira a diva latina máxima: vai do merengue ao reggaeton, da música "tejana" ao funk, com pinceladas de vários elementos latino-americanos.

Tudo isso, claro, com uma roupagem pop. Ela faz as vezes de mulher romântica e sensual, organiza um Carnaval no palco, dança coladinho, entoa baladas melodramáticas com uma banda de mariachis, e por aí vai. Até para nós brasileiros, nem sempre alinhados aos hermanos, tudo soa familiar.

Karol pertence à linhagem de artistas (como Bad Bunny, por exemplo) que provaram que não é preciso abrir mão da própria identidade, nem do próprio idioma, para se consolidar a nível global.

Mesmo cantando majoritariamente em espanhol e se atendo às suas raízes latinas, Karol enche estádios, tem parcerias com artistas do calibre de Shakira e Bruno Mars. Neste momento, ela tem a música mais ouvida do Spotify global ("Bby Wow").

Afinal, até mesmo os EUA, essa hegemonia global, têm uma população latina numerosa. Esse público quer se ver nos palcos, e quer ver sua cultura exaltada — não apagada, principalmente considerando o momento político global.

Isso ficou claro nesse show, em que tudo o que Karol dizia era recebido com gritaria. E em pleno território estadunidense, ela não falou sequer uma frase em inglês.

Karol G em show no Metlife Stadium, em Nova York, no dia 17 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Henry Hwu

Não precisou: em um momento do show, reconheceu no público as bandeiras do México, Argentina, Colômbia, Venezuela, República Dominicana, Nicarágua e até do Brasil.

Em coletiva de imprensa, Karol reforçou que essa era a ideia: representar esse público tão diverso, de uma cultura tão rica, para que todos se vissem na personagem da "tropicoqueta". "Principalmente nesse momento político em que vivemos".

O show tem muitos momentos que falam a língua dos brasileiros. Tem o remix de "Tá OK" do Dennis e Kevin O Chris, "Bandida Entrenada" (composta com Wiu e Tropkillaz), além de diversos momentos de dança com funk e até um quê de Carnaval.

É uma forma dela aproveitar o que temos de energia, mas também uma tentativa de superar um desafio mercadológico que ainda existe para a cantora. O Brasil é a única grande barreira que falta pra Karol: ela ainda não conquistou o público brasileiro como conquistou os latinos lá fora. Afinal, o Brasil é mesmo um mercado difícil para artistas que cantam em espanhol.

Não à toa, o show dela por aqui será na Arena Pacaembu, que tem cerca de metade da capacidade do Metlife Stadium.

Como a própria Karol revelou na coletiva com o g1, ela entende que há um processo para se consolidar por aqui. Ao longo de suas várias vindas, que incluem uma passagem pelo Rock in Rio, ela vem fazendo esse trabalho de formiguinha. Daqui até fevereiro, tem um caminho — segundo ela, com muitas surpresas na manga.

articles.title: Macklemore lança turnê Palestina Livre após polêmica com Ed Sheeran | G1
articles.standfirst: Rapper fará três apresentações em outubro na Europa e promete destinar a organizações de apoio aos palestinos todo o lucro obtido com os shows.
articles.summary: Macklemore fará shows na Europa e doará o lucro da turnê Palestina Livre para apoiar palestinos após ser afastado das apresentações de Ed Sheeran.
articles.body:
Um dos locais que também proibiu Macklemore de se apresentar foi o Raymond James Stadium, na Flórida — Foto: Getty Images/Via BBC

O rapper americano Macklemore anunciou, nesta quinta-feira (24), que organizará sua própria turnê: "Free Palestine Tour", após ser afastado dos shows de Ed Sheeran por suas declarações em apoio aos palestinos.

Sua exclusão como atração de abertura da "Loop Tour", do astro pop britânico, depois de gritar "Palestina Livre!" durante um show em Nova Jersey provocou uma forte polêmica nos Estados Unidos e no exterior.

Em reação, Macklemore anunciou que fará três shows no fim de outubro em Londres, Paris e Dublin. Ele também planeja outros shows nos EUA e disse que todo o lucro será destinado a associações pró-Palestina.

"O que aconteceu comigo é algo maior do que um único artista ou um único palco", disse o rapper de 43 anos em uma publicação no Instagram.

"Quando a classe bilionária pode decidir quais vozes têm permissão para subir ao palco e quais são perigosas demais para serem ouvidas, todo mundo deveria estar prestando atenção. Estamos em 2026. Ser apolítico durante um genocídio não funciona mais", disse.

"As pessoas estão pedindo que os artistas se posicionem, que se informem e que estejam em comunidade. Que usem o palco para algo além do entretenimento. Que resistam quando o chamado a um Palestina livre enfrenta tentativas de silenciamento", acrescentou.

A decisão suscitou uma série de críticas a Ed Sheeran, um dos cantores mais ouvidos de sua geração, que até então despertava amplo consenso.

Durante um show na Filadélfia no último fim de semana, o compositor britânico reconheceu "erros" e declarou que a situação em Gaza era "injustificável".

Outros artistas deixaram a turnê de Sheeran em solidariedade a Macklemore, entre eles Finneas, irmão e colaborador da premiada artista Billie Eilish.

articles.title: Tiffani Thiessen says she ‘got nothing’ for “Saved by the Bell”, didn’t make ‘real money’ until “90210”
articles.summary: Playing Kelly Kapowski made Thiessen famous but not rich.
articles.body:
Tiffani Thiessen said she received low pay for her turn as Kelly on Saved by the Bell .

Her financial picture improved, though, when she joined the cast of Beverly Hills, 90210 , in 1994.

Thiessen's former costar Mark-Paul Gosselaar has also commented on what the teen stars were paid on the '90s show.

Saved by the Bell was big for Tiffani Thiessen 's career, but not for her bank account.

The actress, who played Homecoming Queen Kelly Kapowski on multiple seasons of the teen comedy, confirmed in a recent interview with SiriusXM's Page Six Radio that she and her castmates "got nothing," not even an early peek at episodes.

She added, "We made nothing and we just did our job."

The sitcom starred Thiessen alongside Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Elizabeth Berkley, Mario Lopez, Lark Voorhies, Dennis Haskins, and the late Dustin Diamond between 1989 and 1992.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

"When we went primetime for one season, we got a little bit more," the actress said. "But yeah, I didn't start making real money until I went to 90210 ."

Thiessen went on to portray bad girl Valerie Malone on teen drama Beverly Hills, 90210 between its fifth and ninth seasons. By the time she joined the cast of the popular series, star Shannen Doherty was out, but the rest of the cast, which included Jason Priestley, Luke Perry, Jennie Garth, Tori Spelling, Brian Austin Green, and more, was intact.

In fact, Thiessen and Berkley missed some of Saved by the Bell' s later episodes — without explanation to viewers — because producers had already filmed a graduation, which was ostensibly the end of the show. Thiessen was already off to create problems for Priestley's Brandon Walsh and his friends.

But as for the money coming in because of her sitcom? Well, Thiessen said that she can relate to those posts actors make about receiving minuscule checks for residuals.

"That's exactly right," Thiessen said. "There's actually a funny place, I don't even know if it's still open, called Residuals in L.A., where actors could come in and take their 38 cent check and buy a drink with it."

She said she doesn't think she receives residuals for playing Kelly these days.

"I think it's dried out now," said Thiessen, whose new show is supernatural teen drama Coven Academy . "It costs more to print the check."

Thiessen isn't the only one who's spoken up about the low salaries the teen acts were given in the '90s.

In January 2019, Gosselaar explained on Watch What Happens Live that the Saved by the Bell cast "made really bad deals."

He added, "Poor deals, back then. It is what it is. You move on, you learn. Great experience."

articles.title: Rob Lowe explains why he was ‘the only person happy’ when Will Smith slapped Chris Rock at the Oscars
articles.summary: Lowe was part of an infamously bad Oscars show in 1989.
articles.body:
Rob Lowe did an infamously bad song and dance number at the 1989 Oscars.

When he saw Will Smith slap Chris Rock in 2022, he hoped people would forget what he'd done.

Lowe was then a teen heartthrob who'd performed with Snow White.

Rob Lowe is still humiliated over the, um, musical number that he performed at the 1989 Oscars.

"The worst opening ever," Lowe said Thursday on SiriusXM's Andy Cohen Live . "When Will Smith slapped Chris Rock, I was the only person happy. Because I was like, 'Oh, good. So now that's the worst moment in Oscar history.' But it turns out not really. Turns out I still am dragged, dragged every year."

Smith infamously walked up to Oscars host Chris Rock during the live broadcast of the 2022 event and slapped him across the face after Rock made an unscripted joke about Smith's wife, Jada Pinkett Smith. Ever the professional, Rock continued with the show following the incredulous moment seen by millions of viewers at home.

Rock joked that Pinkett Smith would soon be starring in the sequel to G.I. Jane, the 1997 movie in which Demi Moore's character sported a shaved head. Pinkett Smith has been open about her experience with the hair loss condition alopecia.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

Lowe had his own terrible moment on the Oscars stage back in 1989, as he and Snow White — yes, the princess — performed "Proud Mary" with a cinematic twist.

"This year even, I guess some people didn't love some of the Emmys and they were like, 'At least it wasn't Rob,'" Lowe told Cohen. "It's like, guys, there should be a statute of limitations."

As Lowe has recounted, he did get positive feedback from a comedy great.

"Lucy came up to me afterwards," he noted, "and said, 'Young man, I didn't know you were such a wonderful singer.'"

He's also had John Fogerty, the writer of "Proud Mary," as a guest on his own podcast, Literally! With Rob Lowe .

"John Fogerty was watching it at home," Lowe said. "And he liked it. He forgave me."

And it's not fading away from our collective memories.

In 2018, Entertainment Weekly wrote an oral history of the bizarre entertainment at the 1989 gala.

"The Rob Lowe thing with Snow White was so painful," actress and former talk show host Ricki Lake, who was in another part of the show, said, "like a car accident that you can't look away from."

Don't Tell Mom the Babysitter's Dead actor Keith Coogan was embarrassed by his own participation but grateful for Lowe's gaffe.

"Thankfully people don't necessarily remember our nine minutes," he said.

Lowe's latest project is his movie The Musical , in which he did not sing.

articles.title: Jane Doe Who Accused Jay-Z of Sexual Assault Fully Recants: ‘No Truth to Any of My Claims’
articles.summary: The woman submitted a declaration in Jay-Z’s malicious prosecution lawsuit and was dropped as a defendant by the Roc Nation mogul
articles.body:
The Jane Doe who accused Jay-Z of sexual assault in a startling lawsuit two years ago has now fully recanted her allegations, saying in a new court declaration that her claims were false, that she never met the Roc Nation mogul, and that she had disclosed certain "mental health conditions" to her legal team before they publicly named the Grammy-winning rapper in her lawsuit in December 2024.

"Shawn 'Jay-Z' Carter never raped me. I have never met or spoken to Mr. Carter. Mr. Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever," the woman wrote in the 12-page declaration filed in Manhattan federal court and obtained by Rolling Stone .

"There is no truth to any of my claims against Mr. Carter," she continued under penalty of perjury. "I understand my false accusations have caused Mr. Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone."

The lengthy declaration was filed Thursday along with a notice that Carter was voluntarily dismissing the woman as a defendant in his ongoing malicious-prosecution lawsuit against prominent lawyer Tony Buzbee and his Texas-based law firm. The Jane Doe said she was not promised and did not receive any compensation for the declaration.

"Our client maintains that she was a victim of sexual assault, but she was entirely mistaken in her allegations identifying Mr. Carter, and those allegations were false," Jane Doe's new lawyer in the malicious prosecution case, James Blair Newman, Jr., said in a statement. "Mr. Carter did not rape her, sexually assault her, engage in any inappropriate conduct towards her, and she has never met him. She sincerely and unconditionally apologizes to Mr. Carter and his family."

The new declaration and dismissal filings came more than a year after Carter first sued the woman and her lawyers in federal court. He accused them of conspiring to pressure him into a secret financial settlement "under the threat of devastating harm to his reputation."

Carter's federal court lawsuit was a response to a different lawsuit first filed by the woman in October 2024 that accused Sean "Diddy" Combs of raping her when she was 13 and alleged that an unidentified "male celebrity" also sexually assaulted her. In his filings, Carter has claimed Buzbee sent him an "extortionate demand letter" in November 2024, and, after he refused to pay, amended the lawsuit in December 2024 to identify Carter as the previously unnamed celebrity defendant.

Carter vehemently denied the rape allegation when it became public and revealed he already had sued Buzbee for extortion in California state court in November 2024 using a John Doe pseudonym. In a sworn declaration, he said the demand letter felt like an "existential threat."

"I felt that Mr. Buzbee was placing a gun to my head that I either bow to his demands or endure personal and financial ruin. His actions caused me mental anguish about the ticking time bomb and what it would do to me, my family, and my hard-earned reputation," Carter wrote.

Jane Doe went on to voluntarily dismiss her entire complaint against Carter and Combs in early 2025, admitting there were inconsistencies in her story . A judge later dismissed Carter's Caliifornia-based extortion lawsuit. An appeals court recently upheld that dismissal, finding that Buzbee's demand letter was protected because it was sent in anticipation of filing a lawsuit .

"The record contains no evidence Buzbee accused Carter of raping Jane Doe while knowing those statements to be false or with reckless disregard as to whether they were true. To the contrary, Buzbee submitted declarations showing his firm's and [a referral firm's] investigations led him to subjectively believe in the truth of the accusations," Associate Justice Anne Richardson wrote in the unanimous ruling from California's Second Appellate District earlier this month.

The California ruling leaves Carter's malicious-prosecution lawsuit in New York as his remaining case against Buzbee and his firm. Carter alleges they should have known before filing the Jane Doe lawsuit that her claims "were contradicted by publicly available information, internally inconsistent, and unsupported by any credible story or investigation."

Reached by email late Thursday, Buzbee said he had not seen Jane Doe's new declaration. "We have multiple lawyers (at least four) who dealt with Ms. Doe long before she met me. She gave the exact same story to each. If for some reason now she is claiming she lied to us and the court, that's new information," he wrote. He previously told Rolling Stone that "sending a basic demand letter prior to filing suit is not and will never be 'extortion.'"

In her new declaration, the Jane Doe said her legal claim started when she responded to a Facebook ad in late September or early October 2024 looking for people with sexual assault claims against Sean Combs.

"The ad triggered memories of being raped when I was 13 years old," she claimed in the new filing. She said she clicked on the ad, filled out a form, and received a call asking for more information. She recalled stating during the call that she was a model who attended an afterparty following the Teen Choice Awards in 2000 in New York City. Her lawsuit later claimed the show was the MTV Video Music Awards.

The woman said that her initial October 2024 lawsuit against Combs was filed without her knowledge and without her lawyers "conducting any independent investigation, background inquiry, or due diligence." She further alleged she was given $1,200 in cash by her lawyers when she traveled to Houston in December 2024 for an interview with NBC News. She said her lawyers asked her to take a polygraph test after the news interview due to discrepancies in her story. She never received the results of the test, she claimed

"In January 2025, I began to doubt my claims against Mr. Carter. I also began doubting that I ever went to a party with celebrities," she wrote. After she expressed the doubts to her lawyers, they let her know they were dismissing her lawsuit, she claimed.

In his email to Rolling Stone , Buzbee said he believed Jane Doe received "some petty cash" for meals and travel expenses. "With respect to court filings, each was explained in detail to Ms. Doe, to include the original demand letter. She has previously acknowledged that," he wrote.

In a Sept. 1 motion to dismiss Carter's malicious-prosecution claims, Buzbee and his co-counsel called the lawsuit "improper" and "abusive." They argued that filing a civil complaint on behalf of a Jane Doe alleging sexual assault did not amount to misconduct and that inconsistencies in the woman's recollection were not necessarily suspicious, particularly given her claim that she had been drugged and raped more than two decades earlier, when she was 13.

"This case is itself a malicious prosecution," they argued, referring to Carter's lawsuit.

Combs' lawyers separately denied the woman's allegations, saying he "never sexually assaulted or trafficked anyone — man or woman, adult or minor." Buzbee, meanwhile, continues to represent other plaintiffs pursuing civil claims against Combs.

articles.title: Dabiz Muñoz, chef, sobre el secreto de la puntilla crujiente: "Freír un huevo se puede hacer muy bien o muy mal"
articles.standfirst: Fuego vivo y mucho aceite: así fríe los huevos el mejor chef del mundo
articles.summary: Fuego vivo y mucho aceite: así fríe los huevos el mejor chef del mundo
articles.body: En la gastronomía de alta cuna, los platos más sencillos suelen convertirse en los verdaderos exámenes de maestría profesional. Lejos de las elaboraciones complejas y las esferificaciones de vanguardia, el laureado cocinero madrileño Dabiz Muñoz ha defendido en reiteradas ocasiones la importancia técnica que encierra esta icónica preparación. A través de sus perfiles oficiales en redes sociales y sus apariciones en televisión, el triestrellado chef de 'DiverXO' ha querido desmitificar la aparente simplicidad de la sartén cotidiana para mostrar su visión exacta del resultado ideal. Para el cocinero de la capital, el dilema no admite medias tintas ni titubeos cuando se trata de definir la textura idónea del plato. Él mismo ha declarado abiertamente su devoción absoluta por el método tradicional más crujiente y sabroso: "Me flipan los huevos fritos en mucho aceite de oliva humeante con puntilla bien tostada y muy crujiente. El resto de la clara no muy hecha y la yema cocinada, pero cremosa, que no líquida", dijo en la revista 'Men's Health'. Lograr ese punto impecable exige seguir con absoluta precisión una serie de exigentes pautas técnicas frente al fuego. Muñoz advierte que una de las mayores claves reside en controlar la paciencia durante los primeros instantes del cocinado en la sartén. En sus lecciones audiovisuales durante una entrevista en 'Lecturas' recomendó el paso crucial para conseguir ese dorado distintivo: "El secreto es aguantar un poco hasta tocarlo para que nos quede bien de puntillita". No obstante, las precauciones con el producto deben comenzar antes incluso de rozar la grasa hirviendo. El chef aconseja cascar el huevo en un recipiente aparte para volcarlo suavemente, recordando siempre a sus seguidores que la destreza lo es todo en este proceso: "Freír un huevo se puede hacer muy bien o muy mal". Rociar aceite caliente sobre la clara y salar en el plato completan la fórmula de un proceso que apenas debe prolongarse unos veinte segundos. Asimismo, esta pasión por la fritura perfecta no es algo fortuito, sino un sincero homenaje a los maestros de la gastronomía de antaño. En un emotivo vídeo publicado en sus redes, el cocinero dedicó esta clásica preparación al célebre chef Abraham García diciendo afectuosamente: "Abraham. Esto va por ti". Una muestra clara de que el huevo frito, tratado con rigor, continúa siendo una joya culinaria inolvidable.

articles.title: Jordi Cruz, chef, desvela la receta que nunca falla: "Mis macarrones son muy facilones y llevan muy pocos ingredientes"
articles.standfirst: El toque secreto de un cocinero estrella Michelin para revolucionar tus macarrones con carne
articles.summary: El toque secreto de un cocinero estrella Michelin para revolucionar tus macarrones con carne
articles.body: La pasta es un plato comodín en cualquier hogar, pero lograr que una receta sencilla alcance el nivel de la alta cocina exige técnica y equilibrio. El laureado chef Jordi Cruz, galardonado con estrellas Michelin, ha compartido abiertamente su truco para salir victorioso cuando toca alimentar a un gran número de comensales. Para el cocinero catalán, la clave de una elaboración perfecta radica en las proporciones y en el cuidado tratamiento de la materia prima. El primer paso fundamental comienza al establecer las medidas exactas de la receta. Jordi Cruz lo tiene muy claro cuando prepara sus aclamados macarrones: "Mis macarrones SOS de supervivencia son muy facilones y llevan muy pocos ingredientes. Para kilo y medio de carne, un kilo de macarrones y un kilo de pulpa de tomate", contó en 'Cienradios'. Con esta contundente base, uno de los miembros del jurado de MasterChef asegura el volumen suficiente para satisfacer a toda la mesa sin perder intensidad. El tratamiento de la carne picada dentro del sofrito resulta vital para potenciar el sabor antes de incorporar los líquidos. Para conseguir esa textura dorada indispensable que carameliza la superficie, el cocinero recomienda trabajar a máxima potencia: "Kilo y medio de carne de ternera, subimos el fuego a toda castaña y doramos hasta que el agua se seque y empiece a ponerse doradita y a chisporrotear". La paciencia al hacer el guiso constituye otro factor determinante para que el tomate reduzca de manera óptima. Jordi Cruz advierte que no hay que precipitarse y que conviene bajar la llama gradualmente: "Bajamos el fuego y dejaremos unos 45 minutos que guise suave". Asimismo, para otorgar un extra de cremosidad y matizar la acidez, sugiere sumar un ingrediente poco convencional en la boloñesa tradicional: "Los macarrones con tomate más ricos no solo llevan carne picada, añade 500 ml de leche para hacerlos más cremosos". Por último, el chef destaca la importancia de cuidar el punto exacto de la pasta antes del toque final de horneado o integrado: "Cuece la pasta 2 o 3 minutos menos de lo que indique el fabricante. Utiliza abundante agua con sal y reserva un poco del agua de cocción por si necesitas ajustar la textura de la salsa al final". Con esta sencilla guía llena de pasión, el cocinero demuestra que la excelencia gastronómica también habita en los platos de diario.

articles.title: Taylor Swift has a message for the haters on her new song 'Cleveland!'
articles.summary: Swift, who dropped a deluxe version of her latest album on Friday, included an ode to her husband, Travis Kelce.
articles.body:
Taylor Swift has returned to many of the same themes in her songwriting throughout her 20-year career, from enduring love to brutal breakups to the toxicity of fame. And even as she has ascended to one of the most powerful stars in the world, Swift can never resist one of her favorite topics: Sending a message to her haters.

In 2010's "Mean," she called out a music critic for his harsh commentary and labeled him a pathetic loser. In 2014's "Shake It Off," she waved away the haters who are always gonna hate. In 2017's "Look What You Made Me Do," she mocked the negative comments about her on the internet. In 2019's "I Forgot That You Existed," she triumphed over a nemesis. In 2024's "But Daddy I Love Him," she skewered "wine moms" who judge her relationships.

The list goes on, and Friday, Swift added a new track to the canon. She released four new songs as part of a deluxe edition of her 2025 album, "The Life of a Showgirl," which shattered records last fall when it sold 4 million copies in its first week. The song in question is called, of all things, "Cleveland!"

Your weekly guide to culture, entertainment, and what everyone is talking about. Sign up for free

When the extended track list dropped this week, the title caught people's attention. If it wasn't a "30 Rock" reference (after all, everyone wants to flee to the Cleve), the song obviously had to be about Swift's new husband, Travis Kelce, who grew up in Cleveland Heights. Kelce recently purchased a $5.35 million lakefront mansion that's a short drive away from his old neighborhood. Plus, when Swift appeared on Kelce's podcast last year, she referred to him as a "human exclamation point."

Kelce indeed gets some shout-outs, though not before Swift starts the track — co-written with her longtime collaborators Max Martin and Shellback — by ticking off a list of critiques that are frequently leveled at her online: About her physical appearance; her limited dancing ability; how she's not a "girl's girl" who supports other women; and her style choices. ("With all of that money, why's she dressed like trash?" Swift sings.)

In the chorus, however, Swift declares that none of that nasty commentary matters — because she found her soulmate who likes her just the way she is: "He already took me to Cleveland and showed me the Heights," she taunts. "So hate all you like, this is the love of my life."

Swift lists a few more criticisms in the second verse and how her man ignores them ("Must not have read that scathing take about how I'm fake"), culminating with a spoken word bridge. "You only need to find one person in this entire world who doesn't find you completely insufferable," Swift says. "And I have an important announcement to make … I found mine!" Later, she adds, "Now I'm wearing white !"

As early reaction from fans streamed in, "Cleveland!" was instantly divisive, which could inspire Swift's future hater-themed lyrics.

Although "Cleveland!" will receive plenty of attention, Swift poured even more resources into another deluxe album song, "Patient Zero." She recently teased that a "Patient Zero" music video, starring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell, will debut Sunday during the MTV Video Music Awards.

articles.title: Festival 'shines a light' on Scotland's book town Wigtown
articles.summary: A range of local, national and international authors head to Wigtown for its annual literary celebration.
articles.body:
The annual celebration of literature has started in Scotland's national book town.

The Wigtown Book Festival runs across 10 days until 4 October.

It promises national and international guests while also showcasing Galloway to a wider audience.

More than 250 events are taking place featuring - among others - comedian Lucy Porter, actor Sam Heughan and crime writers Louise Welsh and Chris Brookmyre.

I found the book lover's dream holiday in Scotland

Could visiting book lovers boost our towns' high streets?

The first festival was held in the Dumfries and Galloway town back in 1998 after it won a national competition to become Scotland's book town.

It was up against five other places, Gatehouse of Fleet and Moffat in Dumfries and Galloway as well as Dalmellington, Dunblane and Strathaven.

Since then it has seen a stream of writers, celebrities and politicians drawn to the quiet rural corner of south-west Scotland.

In the process, they have helped give a new life to the town which had seen a string of job losses as major employers closed their doors.

Bookseller and author Shaun Bythell has been part of most of the festivals and has seen the difference they have made.

"I've seen the crucial role it plays - attracting visitors, showcasing Wigtown as Scotland's national book town and in highlighting the literature, culture and history of the region," he said.

"It's so much more than just a book festival – and it's about so much more than books.

"The whole community works together to welcome visitors and to show them all that Wigtown and Galloway have to offer."

Festival programmer Lee Randall said the area was home to many superb contemporary writers of its own.

"The festival programme shines a light on all this as well as the region's wider creativity, culture and environment," she added.

"We are very much looking forward to welcoming visitors for 10 days of literature, film, music, theatre, guided walks and discovery."

articles.title: Aitana rememora su accidente con un corsé en un concierto: “Se podía haber roto completamente y me hubiese quedado en sujetador”
articles.standfirst: La cantante ha concedido una entrevista a Vogue
articles.summary: La cantante ha concedido una entrevista a Vogue
articles.body: En ocasiones, los conciertos pasan de ser un disfrute para los artistas a todo un drama que busca ser terminado lo antes posible. Esto puede ocurrir por caídas encima del escenario, fans que no están en consonancia con lo que escuchan o vestimentas que se convierten en trapos por los movimientos de los artistas. Esto es lo que le pudo pasar a Aitana en uno de sus últimos eventos, al rasgársele un corsé y dejando partes de su cuerpo a la vista de todo el mundo. La cantante ha hablado sobre este episodio en una entrevista para Vogue, en la que ha mostrado el estado en el que quedó la indumentaria que llevaba puesta en dicho concierto. “Este me parece muy icónico por el simple hecho de que se rompiese el corsé. Hubo un look que se nos rompió la tela del corsé, son cosas que pueden pasar, pero claro, yo estaba en el escenario y de repente me giro y dije ‘ostras, que se me está rompiendo el corsé’, y claro, era una imagen que quedaba hasta graciosa”, explicaba la cantante mientras mostraba el atuendo. Sin embargo, no pudo evitar sentir una parte de preocupación al ver el estado de la ropa mientras seguía adelante su show: “Pero claro, cada vez que te mueves se te va rompiendo un poco más, entonces se podía haber roto completamente y me quedaba en sujetador, pero bueno, no se hubiera visto nada muy loco”. Evidentemente, esa pieza no iba a aguantar mucho tiempo, por lo que el equipo de Aitana tuvo que tomar una decisión de emergencia: “Tuve que salir y me tuvieron que coser el corsé. Estaba todo el mundo muy agobiado”, explica la artista, aunque reconoce que le garantizaban que no se iba a quedar desnuda. Para concluir, Aitana desveló que le trajeron otra indumentaria que ya había usado anteriormente, pero ella se negó al cambio: “No voy a quitarme este look que me encanta. Lo arreglamos un momento con la máquina y salgo”.

articles.summary: A proposed salon and spa at Ajay Devgn and Kajol’s Juhu property has become the centre of a dispute involving local residents and the civic authorities.
articles.body: A proposed salon and spa at Ajay Devgn and Kajol’s Juhu property has become the centre of a dispute involving local residents and the civic authorities. According to a Mumbai Mirror report, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has stepped in after the housing society associated with the area raised objections to work being carried out at the bungalow.The dispute revolves around the proposed commercial activity at the property and whether the necessary permissions for such use are in place.What triggered the BMC noticeThe Kapol Co-operative Housing Society reportedly brought the matter to the attention of the BMC after noticing work at the property. The civic body subsequently examined the premises under its K-West ward.As reported by Mumbai Mirror, according to civic officials, the records available to them did not show the required approval for using the premises for commercial purposes. Local corporator Sudha Singh said, “The issue is with the Building and Factory Department of K-West ward. Prima facie, no permission was granted for commercial use of the S-10 premises.”The authorities then sought documentation from the owners to establish whether the proposed activity had received the necessary clearances. With the required papers reportedly not being furnished at that stage, the BMC issued a stop-work notice.The Devgn family has sought four weeks to respond to the notice and provide its documents to the civic authorities.Why the housing society has objectedThe bungalow is located at Plot S-10 on N S Road No. 11 in the JVPD Scheme and reportedly measures around 7,802 sq ft.The residents’ concerns are reportedly linked specifically to the planned commercial activity. The issue, according to the report, is not the fact that the property may have been leased, but what it is intended to be used for.Residents have reportedly expressed apprehension about the impact of a salon and spa on the surrounding residential neighbourhood. Increased footfall, parking, security and noise are among the concerns raised, particularly given the relatively narrow internal roads in the area.Devgn camp contests permission concernsThere are differing positions on whether the proposed use has the necessary approvals. While Ruchi Kanojiya, chief legal and compliance officer at the Devgn Group, was unavailable for comment, a person familiar with the actor’s side maintained that the requisite clearances had already been secured.“The requisite permissions and approvals from the concerned authorities in relation to the proposed use of the premises have been duly obtained,” the person said.The next step will depend on the documents submitted by the property owners and the BMC’s assessment of those approvals. articles.summary: HYDERABAD: The annual auction of the famed Balapur Ganesh laddu fetched a record Rs 39 lakh during the Ganesh Visarjan celebrations in Rangareddy on
articles.body: HYDERABAD: The annual auction of the famed Balapur Ganesh laddu fetched a record Rs 39 lakh during the Ganesh Visarjan celebrations in Rangareddy on Friday.Sam Praneeth Reddy, a 35-year-old businessman from Vanasthalipuram associated with Arban Reality Group, won the prestigious 21-kg Balapur Ganesh laddu with a bid of Rs 39 lakh, news agency ANI reported.Thousands of devotees attended the annual auction. After the final bid, Reddy celebrated the win by posing with the Balapur Ganesh laddu.Reddy recently returned to India from the United States and started his business under the name 'Arban Groups'. He secured the winning bid against eight other participants in the auction.Last year, Lingala Dasharath Goud won the laddu for Rs 35 lakh.The practice of auctioning the laddu, which is considered auspicious by people in the area, began in 1994. It was bought for just Rs 450 in the first auction, and the tradition has continued every year, ANI reported.A portion of the auction proceeds is kept aside for Ganesh Puja celebrations the following year, while the remaining amount is used by organisers for developmental programmes in the Balapur area.Meanwhile, the grand Shoba Yatra in Balapur village has begun, with devotees set to immerse Lord Ganesha's idol to mark the conclusion of Ganesh Chaturthi.Earlier, VHP National Spokesperson Ravinuthala Shashidhar expressed his excitement over the Balapur Shobha Yatra.Talking to ANI, he said, "The public has gathered on the streets, prepared to welcome the Lord. Comprehensive arrangements have been made for this mass immersion event; the government, the administration, and the police department have taken appropriate decisions and put proper systems in place.”“Devotees are participating in an atmosphere of patriotic fervour, helping to carry our culture forward. The event is about to start; although there is a delay of about an hour, the immersion is expected to be completed by 2 PM. There is great enthusiasm surrounding the Balapur Ganesh," he added.Ganesh Chaturthi marks the celebration of Lord Ganesha's birth and is observed with the installation of idols, prayers, devotional offerings and festive gatherings.The festival is particularly prominent in Maharashtra, where elaborate public celebrations and processions are organised.The immersion processions are being held amid security arrangements by local authorities and police to facilitate the movement of devotees and ensure public safety, ANI reported.Leaders and organisers have also appealed to people to follow directions issued by authorities and maintain a peaceful atmosphere during the concluding celebrations.With the immersion marking the culmination of the festivities, devotees across Maharashtra and other parts of the country are participating in processions and offering prayers before bidding farewell to Lord Ganesha.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: In 2002, Jim Carrey bought a Malibu beach house for $9.75 million; 11 years later, he sold the 2,866-sq-ft property for $13.4 million
articles.summary: Discover the journey of Jim Carrey's Malibu beach house, from its $9.75 million purchase to a $13.4 million sale, and the luxurious features that made it a Hollywood gem.
articles.body: Jim Carrey has had a long list of memorable Hollywood homes, but his Malibu beach house stood out for its location. The actor-comedian bought the 2,866-square-foot home in Malibu Colony in 2002 for $9.75 million. At the time, Carrey was already a major Hollywood name, known for films such as 'Ace Ventura' and 'The Truman Show'.Eleven years later, Carrey sold the Malibu property for $13.4 million. The Los Angeles Times reported the sale in June 2013 and said public records showed Carrey had bought the house for $9.75 million in 2002.Jim Carrey bought his Malibu beach house in 2002Carrey bought the Malibu Colony property in 2002, leaving behind his days as a renter in Venice, according to an earlier LA Times report by Ruth Ryon. That report described the home as a refurbished and expanded mid-century modern house with lots of glass, limestone flooring, a rooftop deck and around 30 feet of beach frontage.The later report on the sale listed the property at 2,866 square feet, with five bedrooms and 5.5 bathrooms. It was a two-story contemporary home with an open-plan living room, family room, dining room and kitchen.Inside Jim Carrey's 2,866-square-foot Malibu homeThe biggest attraction was obviously the ocean.The living spaces opened onto a deck facing the Pacific, giving the home a very strong indoor-outdoor feel. There were fireplaces in both the living room and master bedroom, while a spa sat on the rooftop deck.When the Malibu house was listed in 2012, E! also highlighted its terrace with adjustable privacy walls, updated kitchen, family room, outdoor entertaining area and rooftop spa. The listing was then asking $13.95 million.The home was part of Malibu Colony, a gated coastal community known for its celebrity residents. Forbes, while covering the most expensive celebrity homes for sale in 2012, noted that Carrey's property occupied about 0.17 acres and had its own stretch of oceanfront.Jim Carrey's Malibu property was listed for much moreCarrey did not sell the home immediately.According to UPI's 2013 report, the Malibu beach house had first been listed in 2011 for $18 million. It was later taken off the market and relisted in 2012 for $13.95 million.The Los Angeles Times also reported the $13.95 million 2012 listing, along with the home's five bedrooms, 5.5 bathrooms, ocean-facing deck and rooftop spa.After spending around two years on the market, Carrey finally sold it for $13.4 million in 2013.Jim Carrey sold his Malibu beach house for $13.4 millionThe final sale price was $13.4 million, according to the Los Angeles Times. Janelle Friedman of Sotheby's International Realty in Pacific Palisades represented Carrey in the deal.UPI also reported the $13.4 million sale and noted that the buyer's identity had not been disclosed publicly at the time.The difference between Carrey's reported purchase price of $9.75 million in 2002 and the final sale price of $13.4 million in 2013 was $3.65 million, before accounting for taxes, maintenance and other costs.From Hollywood comedy star to Malibu homeownerCarrey bought the beach house during a busy period in his acting career. His film credits at the time included 'Ace Ventura', 'The Truman Show' and 'Bruce Almighty', while he would later appear in movies such as 'Mr. Popper's Penguins'.For 11 years, the Malibu Colony home gave Carrey an oceanfront retreat in one of Los Angeles' most exclusive celebrity neighbourhoods.But in 2013, that chapter came to an end. The 2,866-square-foot Malibu beach house that Jim Carrey bought for $9.75 million in 2002 eventually changed hands for $13.4 million, after years of being one of his most talked-about properties.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Alex Warren first headliner for Live at Powderham festival 2027
articles.summary: The booking follows a breakthrough period that saw his album Wildchild top charts in the UK and US.
articles.body:
Grammy award-nominated singer Alex Warren has been announced as the first headliner for a music festival.

Warren will top the bill at Live at Powderham 2027 on 26 June. The four-day music festival, which takes place at Powderham Castle, near Exeter, runs from 24 to 27 June.

Warren's appearance follows a breakthrough period for the US star, whose second album, Wildchild, reached number one in several countries including the UK and US.

His hit single Ordinary became one of the biggest songs of 2025 and helped establish him as one of pop music's fastest-rising artists, said festival organisers.

Peter Taylor, co-founder of festival promoter Cuffe & Taylor, said Warren was a "phenomenal talent and it will be an unforgettable night".

Live at Powderham attracted thousands of music fans in 2026, with headline performances from Lewis Capaldi, Alanis Morissette and Teddy Swims.

articles.summary: Johnny Depp has often spoken about how fatherhood changed his perspective on life.
articles.body: Johnny Depp has often spoken about how fatherhood changed his perspective on life. In one of his reflections, the actor opened up about moving past anger and frustration and learning to appreciate life differently after starting a family.He made the remark while discussing how becoming a father changed his outlook on life. In a 2012 interview with The Sun, he spoke about feeling “empty,” angry and frustrated when he was younger and said the birth of his first child changed the way he appreciated life.Meaning of Johnny Depp’s quoteHis quote reflects on a change in perspective that came with becoming a parent. He says that before starting his family, he often felt angry and frustrated and did not fully appreciate the life he was living but things changed after he became a dad. The important part of the quote is his admission that he “didn’t really appreciate life” before becoming a father.The quote is therefore less about saying that having children automatically makes someone happy and more about personal growth, learnings and how priorities change over time. Depp describes fatherhood as the experience that helped him recognise things he had previously taken for granted.Why Johnny Depp’s quote is relevant todayThe quote continues to resonate because many people can relate to becoming so consumed by frustration, work or personal problems that they overlook the positive aspects of their lives.His words encourage readers to pause and recognise the people and moments that give their lives meaning rather than focusing just on what is going wrong all the time.Early life of Johnny DeppJohnny Depp was born on June 9, 1963, in Owensboro, Kentucky. He became passionate about music at a young age and took up playing guitar. He dropped out of high school at 15 and started to play music with various bands before turning to acting and had early television success, leading to his discovery by the producers of 21 Jump Street.Johnny Depp’s rise to fameDepp’s stardom saw major rise when he began to work with director Tim Burton, and he became a leading star in films such as Edward Scissorhands, Sleepy Hollow and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. articles.summary: In 1996, Denzel Washington and his wife, Pauletta, purchased two Beverly Park lots from Disney chairman Michael Eisner and his wife, Jane, for close to
articles.body: In 1996, Denzel Washington and his wife, Pauletta, purchased two Beverly Park lots from Disney chairman Michael Eisner and his wife, Jane, for close to the $6.5 million asking price, according to the Los Angeles Times. Washington, then 41, personally negotiated the deal with Eisner. The couple, who had four children, planned to build a house on the site overlooking Beverly Hills and hoped to complete it by the following spring. Their existing home in Toluca Lake had suffered damage in the Northridge earthquake. The purchase came as Washington was already an established Hollywood actor, having won the best supporting-actor Oscar for Glory and starred in films including Malcolm X, Philadelphia and Crimson Tide.Denzel Washington negotiated directly with Michael EisnerThe property deal had an unusual detail. Washington personally negotiated the purchase with Eisner, who was Disney's chairman at the time. Sources said Eisner had received higher offers after the properties were already in escrow, but the deal with Washington went ahead. The two lots were in Beverly Park, where Brian Adler had the listing, while Barbara Robinson of John Aaroe & Associates in Beverly Hills represented the Washingtons. The reported price was close to $6.5 million, the asking price for the two lots.The couple planned a new home for their familyWashington and Pauletta had four children when they bought the property and planned to build a house on the two lots overlooking Beverly Hills. The couple hoped to have the new home completed by spring 1997. Their existing home was in Toluca Lake and had suffered damage during the Northridge earthquake, which struck Southern California on January 17, 1994.Washington was already a major Hollywood starAt the time of the purchase, Washington was 41 and had already built a substantial film career. He had won the Academy Award for best supporting actor for Glory, the 1989 film about an African American regiment during the American Civil War. By 1996, his film credits also included Malcolm X, The Pelican Brief, Philadelphia, Crimson Tide, Virtuosity and Devil in a Blue Dress. His upcoming projects included Courage Under Fire, due for release that summer, and The Preacher's Wife, scheduled for December.His work away from Hollywood also made headlinesThe 1996 report also highlighted Washington's charitable activities. In February that year, an outpatient paediatric wing at Martin Luther King Jr./Charles Drew Medical Center was named after him. Later that month, Harvard University held a Hasty Pudding-style reception honouring Washington for his humanitarian work. He was also a national spokesman for the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, an organisation he had been involved with since his youth. The Los Angeles Times noted that he had attended the club in his hometown of Mount Vernon, New York, and donated time and money to charitable causes.The Beverly Park purchase became a long-term homeThe property Washington acquired in 1996 later became associated with the family's Beverly Park residence. Later property reporting has described the Washington estate as a substantial compound with a large main house and additional amenities. Architectural Digest has reported that the Beverly Park property includes a roughly 30,000-square-foot main house, a guesthouse, tennis court and swimming pool. These features reflect the property's later development, while the 1996 purchase involved two lots on which Washington and Pauletta planned to build a new family home.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision?
