articles.title: Abhijeet Sawant says Arijit Singh's rise to fame was pure destiny: 'If you compare him and me at that time, I was very popular, but he wasn't'
articles.summary: Abhijeet Sawant continues to hold a special place, as he had won the first season of 'Indian Idol'.
articles.body: Abhijeet Sawant continues to hold a special place, as he had won the first season of 'Indian Idol'. He clinched the title in the show's debut season back in 2005, and even though several winners have followed him over the years, the level of stardom and public affection he received remains hard to match.Interestingly, the same year saw the channel roll out another talent hunt, 'Fame Gurukul', which featured contestants including Arijit Singh and Qazi Touqueer. While Qazi went on to win that season and is now seen competing on 'Bigg Boss 20', Arijit has since become one of the most celebrated playback voices of his time. In a recent chat, Abhijeet was asked to compare his career graph with Arijit's, and he credited fate for shaping how things unfolded for both of them.Arijit Singh stayed out of the spotlight for a decade, says Abhijeet SawantSpeaking to Filmygyan, Abhijeet Sawant revealed that although he and Arijit Singh both found initial recognition in 2005, their career paths diverged sharply once their respective shows ended. Abhijeet walked away with a cash prize of Rs 1 crore courtesy of 'Indian Idol', along with a music album deal with the channel, quickly turning him into a household name. Arijit, on the other hand, did not land similar opportunities as a singer right away and had to restart his journey from scratch."After 2005, Arijit stayed away from the limelight. For at least 10 years, call it a blessing in disguise, he went to the music studios, and he worked with all the major music composers, not as a singer but as a producer, as a programmer," Abhijeet said, adding, "He went back to the basics, and he started his journey again, and no one knew him back then."Abhijeet also pointed out the stark difference in the kind of public pressure both of them faced during those years, given how much more recognisable he was at the time."If you compare him and me at that time, I was very popular, but he wasn't. So the kind of pressure that I faced was very different than the pressure that he was facing. He worked a lot for those 10 years and worked a lot with musicians, and then he got his first big song."Abhijeet Sawant calls Arijit Singh landing 'Tum Hi Ho' pure destinyWhile Arijit's debut track was 'Dil Sambhal Ja Zara' from 'Murder 2', it was 'Tum Hi Ho' from 'Aashiqui 2' that truly catapulted him into stardom. Abhijeet believes that bagging this particular song was simply meant to be."'Tum Hi Ho' made Arijit 'Arijit Singh', and that song landing in the lap of any singer… It was all about destiny," he said.'Everyone has their own journey,' says Abhijeet SawantWrapping up the conversation, Abhijeet Sawant made an observation about how audiences tend to judge artistes based on visible success, often being quick to criticise those who haven't achieved the same recognition."It is a flaw with the audience that we keep praising the one who is successful, but the ones we don't know much about, we keep finding flaws in them. That's not all. Everyone has their own journey. Everyone is trying their best to work, live their life. Let them," he said.Arijit Singh had announced his retirement from playback singing earlier this year, though he continues to fulfil prior professional commitments, meaning fans can still expect new music from him in upcoming films. articles.title: Inside Travis Kelce’s new home with a past worthy of a Taylor Swift song: A 1904-built Ohio mansion, 21,000 sq ft and a 120-year history
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s new Ohio home is far more than a lavish lakefront property.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s new Ohio home is far more than a lavish lakefront property. The Kansas City Chiefs star has purchased Moyenage, a historic mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio, whose more-than-a-century-old story includes wealthy industrialists, a Sherwin-Williams president, an inventor and even a brief brush with Hollywood history.According to a report by News 5 Cleveland WEWS⁠, Travis reportedly paid $5.35 million for the property in March 2026, according to recent reports. The purchase came around four months before his July wedding to Taylor Swift. The couple had previously been linked to interest in Northeast Ohio, where Kelce and his brother Jason grew up and where the NFL star has longstanding family ties.Located on a 3.5-acre site overlooking Lake Erie, Moyenage is a roughly 21,000-square-foot Elizabethan Tudor mansion. The property includes eight bedrooms and 11 bathrooms, along with a gatehouse and a range of amenities added or restored over the years. Its interiors feature elaborate woodwork, carved lions, leaded-glass doors and an observatory with amber glass skylights.Morse and his wife, Seville Samantha Hanna Pickands, were the mansion’s first owners. The property was designed to reflect the grandeur associated with the wealthy families who built estates along Lake Erie during the period.Its name, Moyenage, comes from a French term referring to medieval times, fitting the home’s Tudor-inspired architecture. The interiors feature beamed ceilings, detailed plasterwork, hand-carved mouldings and a striking black-walnut double staircase with carved lions.After Seville Morse’s estate, the mansion was purchased in 1928 by George A. Martin, who went on to become president of Sherwin-Williams. Martin remained at Moyenage until his death in 1944.The property later belonged to James H. Rand III, an inventor and scientist whose life was equally unusual. According to report by Case Western Reserve University⁠, Rand was credited with numerous inventions and served during World War II, including work with the U.S. Office of Strategic Services. He also established a laboratory in the estate’s former gardener’s cottage across the street.The house even appeared on televisionMoyenage’s history also includes a small piece of television history. In 1962, its entry hall, living room, dining room and bedroom were used during the filming of an episode of the CBS series Route 66. The episode, titled Every Father’s Daughter, aired in November that year.That detail has made the property’s history particularly intriguing, although the mansion’s documented history is much broader than that one chapter.Why it sounds like a Taylor Swift songThe history of Moyenage has inevitably drawn comparisons with Taylor Swift’s fascination with houses, old wealth and the stories attached to them.Swift’s The Last Great American Dynasty famously tells the story of Rebekah Harkness, the wealthy socialite who once owned Swift’s Rhode Island mansion. The song turns the history of a grand home and its former owner into a narrative about money, reputation and the people who lived there before Swift.Moyenage has a similarly layered past. Before Kelce, it belonged to families connected to Cleveland’s industrial and business history, including the president of Sherwin-Williams and an inventor whose life extended from science to wartime service.Recent coverage has also highlighted details that seem almost tailor-made for a Swift reference: a grand doorway featured on television, elaborate lions throughout the entrance and a century-old mansion with stories attached to nearly every chapter of its ownership history.A new chapter for Travis Kelce and Taylor SwiftFor Kelce, the purchase also brings him closer to the area where he grew up. Bratenahl sits just east of Cleveland and is known for its large historic homes along Lake Erie. The village has long attracted prominent businesspeople and celebrities seeking waterfront properties and privacy.The mansion’s reported $5.35 million sale is also significant for the small community. News 5 Cleveland reported that it was the highest recorded home sale in Bratenahl, according to the property’s listing agents.Now, after more than 120 years of changing owners, Moyenage has entered a very different chapter. Its next story belongs to Travis Kelce and, potentially, Taylor Swift, adding two of the world’s most recognisable names to a house that already had plenty of stories of its own.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Ed Sheeran concertgoers warn artists about sharing political views: 'You're going to alienate' fans
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran fans at his Philadelphia concert warned artists that political statements alienate audiences ahead of his Gillette Stadium shows.
articles.body: Several fans who attended Ed Sheeran’s concert in Philadelphia last weekend after Macklemore was dropped for making "Free Palestine" comments, warned other artists that if they make political statements, they will alienate half of their audience. The "Bad Habits" singer is expected to play his second and third concerts since the controversy this Friday and Saturday at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, which is owned by Robert Kraft. The New England Patriots owner allegedly threatened to cancel the concerts at his venue if Macklemore wasn’t taken off the tour, according to the "Thrift Shop" rapper. ROBERT KRAFT, GILLETTE STADIUM BOOT MACKLEMORE FROM ED SHEERAN TOUR OVER ‘FREE PALESTINE’ RANT Macklemore also claimed Kraft got other stadium owners to agree to not allow Sheeran to play at their venues if the rapper was still with his tour. "The fact that they’re forcing Ed Sheeran to have an opinion is not right," one woman told Fox News Digital outside last Saturday’s concert. "He wants to stay in the middle – if you have an opinion, that’s fine, but you’re going to alienate at least 50% of your population, and it causes unrest." GOO GOO DOLLS' JOHN RZEZNIK DRAWS LINE ON POLITICS AT CONCERTS: 'I'M NOT GOING TO LECTURE YOU' She said the "Shape of You" singer "just wants to do his music and play his music, and people want to enjoy it. They want to get away from it, and I don’t feel as though they should have to worry about this stuff when they come to a concert." Macklemore was dropped as the opening act for Sheeran’s tour earlier this month after he made pro-Palestinian comments at two concerts. The other supporting acts on Sheeran’s tour quit in solidarity with Macklemore. LIBERAL LAWMAKERS, ACTIVISTS RALLY BEHIND MACKLEMORE AFTER SHEERAN TOUR REMOVAL OVER 'FREE PALESTINE' STANCE In Philadelphia Saturday night, Sheeran made a nearly four-minute-long speech in which he explained to fans that he never wanted to be an activist musician and that he was there continuing his tour alone because he wanted to honor his commitment to fans. ED SHEERAN FACES GROWING BACKLASH AS RADIO STATION BANS SONGS, PROTEST GROUPS RESPOND TO MACKLEMORE'S REMOVAL He said he can also see both sides of such a complex issue, admitting that he doesn’t know enough about it, is still learning and will make mistakes as he tries to navigate the situation. Another fan told Fox News Digital ahead of the concert last Saturday that, as artists and musicians have a right to speak their mind: "They also don’t have to — they’re entertainment. I have a right to choose to listen or to not listen. I think it’s all about my choice — I live in America, I can decide to ignore or to listen, and they have the same right." GORILLAZ FRONTMAN DAMON ALBARN HOLDS UP PALESTINIAN FLAG DURING SHOW AFTER MACKLEMORE TOUR REMOVAL "It’s a really tough thing," a woman, who told Fox News Digital she is a schoolteacher, said outside the concert. "I am in a classroom every day, and I have my own thoughts on politics in the same way that I’m sure every artist does. I also do not share those with my students because I want them to have a safe space where they are who they are, and I think that’s kind of the same way I want concerts to be. articles.title: Russell takes pole in Baku as Antonelli hits wall
articles.summary: George Russell takes pole position for Mercedes at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashes out.
articles.body:
George Russell took an imperious pole position for Mercedes at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix as his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashed out.

Russell beat Ferrari's Charles Leclerc by a massive 0.837 seconds while Antonelli, who leads the Britain by 81 points in the championship, will start in 16th.

The Italian hit the inside wall at Turn One in the first session and was knocked out.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was third ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar and McLaren's Lando Norris.

Lewis Hamilton, compromised by running without a tow from another car, was sixth, ahead of the Alpine of Pierre Gasly and Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

With a tow or slipstream worth as much as 0.5 seconds, Verstappen was following Norris on their final laps when the Briton made a mistake and went off track.

That scuppered Verstappen's chances of competing at the front.

But although the four-time champion had looked capable of contending for the front row, Russell was in a league of his own.

On a weekend in which Antonelli's running has been compromised by reliability problems that meant he missed out on half the possible running on Thursday, Russell absolutely delivered on Mercedes' dominant position on this unique track.

Russell has looked comfortable all weekend and never looked in danger of being beaten for pole, his first since the Austrian Grand Prix at the end of June.

"That's probably the biggest margin I've had in my whole career," Russell said. "The lap felt really sweet and the car has been feeling great all weekend."

Leclerc was somewhat taken aback by Mercedes' superiority, saying that the position was what he expected but the gap most definitely was not.

At the bottom of the top 10, there was finally some good news for Williams, for whom Carlos Sainz achieved the team's first top 10 qualifying performance of the year.

Williams have introduced a new chassis this weekend which has brought them down to the weight limit for the first time this season, after being as much as 25kg over at the start of the year.

Along with some additional developments, it appears to have produced a big step forwards, although the caveat is that Baku is a track that suits the characteristics of the Williams car and does not expose its weaknesses.

Team-mate Alex Albon did not manage to secure a tow in the second part of qualifying and was 13th, just under 0,4secs behind the Spaniard.

Antonelli's error came on his second lap of the first session.

He turned into the first corner too early, and the left front wheel clouted the inside wall, breaking the suspension.

He initially tried to get the car back to the pits but was told by engineer Peter Bonnington to park up.

"Let me try," Antonelli pleaded, before Bonnington told him that either the track rod or upright was broken and there was no way Mercedes could fix that in the time they had to turn the car around before the next session.

articles.title: Nuria Roca confiesa qué haría si aparece el hombre de sus sueños: "Si ahora mismo viene, allá que voy" y la reacción de Del Val: "Te digo, 'vete"
articles.standfirst: Anécdota de lo más llamativa con los comentarios y sensaciones del matrimonio formado por Nuria y Juan en la tertulia de 'el Hormiguero'
articles.summary: Anécdota de lo más llamativa con los comentarios y sensaciones del matrimonio formado por Nuria y Juan en la tertulia de 'el Hormiguero'
articles.body: Una sorprendente historia de una mujer que estuvo a punto de romper su matrimonio por creer que mantenía una relación con Enrique Iglesias acabó dejando una de las escenas más comentadas de la tertulia de El Hormiguero que implicaba directamente a Nuria Roca y Juan del Val. La protagonista indirecta fue la presentadora valenciana que no dudó en sincerarse cuando Pablo Motos le planteó una pregunta de lo más comprometida. Tras escuchar el caso de esta mujer de 63 años, víctima de una estafa amorosa a través de internet, Motos comentó entre bromas que, de estar en el lugar del marido, no perdonaría la situación. Fue entonces cuando el presentador quiso saber si Roca sería capaz de marcharse con algún famoso que no fuera Juan del Val. La respuesta de la colaboradora fue inmediata y provocó las risas en el plató. "Si ahora mismo Jacob Elordi viene, yo allá que voy", admitió sin pensárselo demasiado al referirse al popular actor australiano. Lejos de molestarse, Juan del Val siguió el juego a su mujer y respondió con total naturalidad: "Yo te digo 'vete'". Incluso animó a Pablo Motos a hacer un llamamiento para que el protagonista de algunas de las series y películas más exitosas de los últimos años visitara el programa. La conversación fue un paso más allá cuando Motos planteó qué ocurriría si Jacob Elordi acudiese algún día a El Hormiguero. Nuria Roca mantuvo su postura y dejó otra frase que provocó carcajadas entre los presentes: "Si viene, yo vengo a verle". Juan del Val tampoco dejó pasar la oportunidad para bromear y remató el momento preguntando si podía unirse a ambos, una ocurrencia que terminó de desatar las risas en el plató. Eso sí, antes de cambiar de asunto, la presentadora quiso matizar sus palabras. Entre risas, explicó que este tipo de confesiones se hacen precisamente porque son situaciones imposibles: "Esto lo digo así porque sé que es imposible. Si sabes que es posible, no lo dices". Una respuesta espontánea de Nuria Roca que volvió a demostrar la complicidad que mantiene con Juan del Val, capaz de convertir cualquier comentario sobre famosos en una divertida anécdota televisiva.

articles.title: Sunita Ahuja says 'kuch Rakshas' are ruining her life; appeals to Gen Z for support amid Govinda - Komal Rani Swarnkar rumours: 'Mera ghar toot raha hai'
articles.summary: Speculation around actor Govinda's personal life has been building for weeks, with reports suggesting he may be involved with his 'Roopa' co-star Komal
articles.body: Speculation around actor Govinda's personal life has been building for weeks, with reports suggesting he may be involved with his 'Roopa' co-star Komal Rani Swarnkar, despite being married to Sunita Ahuja for the past 39 years. These rumours gained further momentum after the two were recently seen together at the Lalbaugcha Raja celebrations in Mumbai. Amid all this, Sunita made a trip to a temple in Kolkata, where she opened up about the "demons" troubling her life and made an emotional plea to the younger generation for their support.Sunita Ahuja's emotional appeal to Gen ZAddressing the media, Sunita Ahuja candidly spoke about the strain in her marriage to Govinda. During her visit to the Dakshineswar Kali temple near Kolkata, she referenced how the Goddess is believed to vanquish evil, saying, "Mere bhi jeevan mein kuch rakshas hain, aur main Mata ke dwara bolne aaye hoon ki unka bhi naash karein (I too have some demons in my life, and I have come here at the behest of Mata to seek their destruction as well)." She explained that her visit was aimed at seeking divine intervention to clear away the obstacles in her life.Sunita went on to allege that the situation was being manufactured for publicity and urged people not to encourage such behaviour. "What would you do if your daughter or daughter-in-law had to go through something like this? I want everyone to support me," she said, further adding, "Jitne bhi Gen Z bacche ho, auratein ho, mujhe support kijiye. Joh mere saath ho raha hai, vo accha nahi ho raha hai. Mera ghar toot raha hai for no reason (To all the Gen Z youngsters and women, please support me. What is happening to me is not right. My home is breaking apart for no reason)."A timeline of the marital trouble rumoursBack in December 2024, reports had surfaced claiming that Sunita had moved to file for divorce from Govinda. By February 2025, the actor's manager acknowledged the couple's separation but insisted that all differences had since been resolved. However, in August this year, amid growing chatter about Govinda's alleged relationship with his co-star, Sunita withdrew her divorce petition.The dating rumours first gained traction when Govinda and Komal were spotted together at the Mumbai airport earlier this year. Following their joint appearance at Lalbaugcha Raja, Govinda addressed the speculation while speaking to ANI, stating, "This is not a subject for anyone, even if there is an affair. I am working and maintaining a professional relationship." He also referenced past temple visits with former co-stars Karisma Kapoor and Raveena Tandon, saying such visits had always brought him good fortune.Govinda and Sunita tied the knot in 1987 and share two children — daughter Tina Ahuja and son Yashvardhan Ahuja.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Gaming’s biggest horror series are more vital than ever
articles.summary: With the release of Silent Hill: Townfall and the new Resident Evil movie reboot, both survival horror franchises are proving their staying power.
articles.body: For the third year in a row, I’ve been scared out of my wits by a new Silent Hill game. First it was the modern remake of Silent Hill 2, then the Japan-set spinoff Silent Hill F. Now I find myself slowly crawling through a quaint Scottish town in Silent Hill: Townfall, trying my best not to get brutally murdered by demonic creatures chasing me through the streets. It’s been a remarkable turnaround for a franchise that once seemed like it was on life support. And when you combine it with a strong run from Resident Evil across games and film, you have gaming’s two biggest horror franchises both at the height of their powers. For Resident Evil, it’s been a steady buildup, but it really started with Resident Evil 7 nearly a decade ago. It jolted the series back to life with a first-person perspective that made its scares feel more visceral. Since then, Capcom has settled on an effective strategy of alternating between bottom-up remakes of classics like Resident Evil 4, and new spins on the formula, like the vampire-tinged Village. This has allowed the studio to be more experimental with the mainline titles; this year’s Requiem, for instance, was a bold attempt to merge two types of Resident Evil games together, mixing straight-up action with first-person terror. [Media: Resident Evil has always had an uneven track record when it comes to adaptations, like the largely forgettable live-action Netflix series. But that may be changing. Last week a reboot of the film series premiered, called simply Resident Evil, helmed by Weapons director Zach Cregger. It explored the zombie franchise from a new viewpoint: Instead of following iconic characters like Leon or Claire, it was centered on a hapless delivery driver who served as a stand-in for a player who is terrible at survival horror games. Like the Exit 8 movie, Resident Evil explores its source material through the lens of the player. The result was equal parts hilarious and horrifying — there were scenes where gore dripped from ceilings, and a particularly terrifying long-limbed baby — and it also had the best box office opening in franchise history. Silent Hill has followed a similar trajectory, albeit on a smaller scale. After lying largely dormant following the 2015 cancellation of Silent Hills, a reboot led by Hideo Kojima and Guillermo del Toro, Konami signaled a return for the franchise with a series of announcements in 2022. Not everything has been a winner — a film came out earlier this year with little fanfare, and the less said about the bizarre interactive TV series Ascension the better — but when it comes to games Silent Hill has been on a roll. The Silent Hill 2 remake set the stage, introducing arguably the most beloved title in the series to a new audience, while Silent Hill F offered a freshly horrifying experience through its setting and more RPG-focused gameplay. [Media: Townfall likewise expands the idea of what a Silent Hill game can be. It launches this week on the PS5 and PC, and is developed by Screen Burn, an indie studio known for games like Observation. You play as a man named Simon who arrives at a small Scottish town where it’s immediately evident something is wrong; it seems completely deserted and is shrouded in the classic Silent Hill fog. Oh yeah, and screeching creatures ripped out of Hellraiser stalk the streets. From there you have to figure out what actually happened, and try your best not to die at the hands of a mutated monstrosity. What’s most notable about Townfall is how it plays. It has much in common with “walking simulator” games like Firewatch and Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture, where the experience is about exploring a space and uncovering a story organically. Here that means poking around in abandoned homes and medical centers, reading through files and listening to phone messages that reveal the extent of the town’s horrific history. The game then layers on more traditional horror elements. There’s some light combat, but mostly there’s a big focus on stealth: to get where you need to go you’ll often have to sneak past unpredictable monsters, who hunt mindlessly while screeching and writhing in pain. This plays out a little like Alien: Isolation; you have a handheld device that tells you where enemies are, and you can hide in closets and sheds in hopes they don’t spot you. It’s incredibly scary, and still feels intrinsically like a Silent Hill game, despite the shifts in gameplay and setting. The triumphant return of Resident Evil and Silent Hill is coming at a particularly exciting time for horror, with breakout successes at the box office and a promising wave of streaming series. The genre is having a moment — and despite being around for decades, both series are hitting a fresh stride at just the right time

articles.title: Quote of the day by Tom Hanks: ‘Show up on time, know your lines, and have an idea in your pocket,’ a simple yet powerful life lesson explaining the importance of preparation and discipline
articles.summary: Discover Tom Hanks' powerful advice on preparation and discipline in both acting and life. Learn how showing up on time, knowing your lines, and contributing ideas can boost your career.
articles.body: A lot of career advice sounds impressive until you actually have to use it. Tom Hanks’ advice is much simpler than that. It is almost blunt: show up, be prepared and bring something of your own.The Hollywood actor learned that lesson when he was just 20 years old, during his early days in theatre. Decades later, he still remembered the words of director Dan Sullivan, who had once lost his patience with a young cast that was tired, unprepared and not quite doing its job.Today’s quote of the day by Tom Hanks reads: “Show up on time, know your lines, and have an idea in your pocket.”What does the quote by Tom Hanks mean?Hanks recalled the story during an appearance on the 'SmartLess' podcast with Jason Bateman, Will Arnett and Sean Hayes. Talking about his early theatre career, he remembered Sullivan telling the actors they had to show up on time, know their lines and have an idea. Hanks said the lesson “really super stuck” with him.The quote is really about three very ordinary things that can make a big difference at work.First, show up on time. It sounds obvious, but being on time tells people that they can rely on you. For Hanks, it was part of understanding that everyone on a production has a job to do and one person being unprepared can affect everyone else.Then comes knowing your lines. For an actor, that literally means knowing the script. But the idea can be applied to almost any job. Know what you are doing. Read the brief. Understand the assignment. Do not walk into a meeting or project expecting someone else to explain everything to you. And then there is the most interesting part: “have an idea in your pocket.”Hanks explained that this meant having something of your own to contribute. It could be an acting choice, a different approach or simply another way of looking at the material. In the same 'SmartLess' conversation, he explained that an actor can suggest something that is not on the page, but also pointed out that if the director says not to do it, you move on.So the quote is not really about trying to take over. It is about not being completely passive.How is the quote by Tom Hanks relevant today?This advice works far beyond acting. For a student, “know your lines” could mean actually preparing before a presentation instead of reading the slides for the first time in class. For someone starting an internship, it could mean understanding the company, reading the brief properly and coming into a meeting with at least one useful thought.And “have an idea in your pocket” might be the most useful part today. Workplaces move quickly, and people are often expected to do more than simply follow instructions. You do not need to have the perfect answer every time. Sometimes having one idea, one question or one possible solution is enough to show that you were paying attention.Hanks’ own story makes the advice more interesting because he was not a famous actor when he learned it. He was a 20-year-old theatre actor still figuring things out.Early life of Tom HanksTom Hanks was born on July 9, 1956, in Concord, California. His parents divorced when he was five, and his family moved around several times before eventually settling in Oakland. He became interested in acting while attending college and eventually transferred to California State University, Sacramento, to study theatre.In 1977, Hanks joined the Great Lakes Shakespeare Festival in Ohio. He spent his summers performing in Shakespeare productions and his winters working backstage at a community theatre in Sacramento.It was during this period that he worked under director Dan Sullivan and picked up the lesson that would stay with him for the rest of his career. Hanks has spoken about those early theatre years as an important part of learning how professional productions actually work. At that point, there was no guarantee that he would become one of Hollywood’s biggest stars. He was simply a young actor trying to get better.How did Tom Hanks rise to fame?Hanks moved to New York after his time with the Great Lakes Shakespeare Festival and began taking on smaller acting jobs. In 1980, he worked in the television sitcom 'Bosom Buddies' and garnered fame.His major breakthrough came with Ron Howard’s 'Splash' in 1984. The success of the film helped establish Hanks as a leading Hollywood actor, and he followed it with movies including 'Big', 'A League of Their Own' and 'Sleepless in Seattle'.His career later took a more dramatic turn with films such as 'Philadelphia', 'Forrest Gump', 'Saving Private Ryan' and 'Cast Away'. Hanks won the Academy Award for Best Actor for 'Philadelphia' and then again for 'Forrest Gump'.But the interesting thing about his career advice is that it does not sound like advice from someone who started at the top. It sounds like something learned backstage, after a long rehearsal, from a director who was tired of watching young actors turn up unprepared. And perhaps that is why the line has lasted.Show up. articles.title: Meghan Markle’s outing with Ellen DeGeneres exposes 'irony' in royal’s ‘quiet country life’: expert
articles.summary: Meghan Markle's first photographed outing in the Cotswolds with Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi raises questions about her quiet life claims.
articles.body: Meghan Markle is raising questions after being photographed in England with two Hollywood stars. The 45-year-old royal was recently photographed in the Cotswolds with Ellen DeGeneres and her wife, Portia de Rossi, in her first photographed outing since arriving in the U.K., which Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered" said hints that "there is already going to be considerably less privacy for Meghan in Britain than perhaps she anticipated." "But there is an irony here too. If Harry and Meghan genuinely wanted to disappear into quiet country life, the Cotswolds is one of the places where they could probably accomplish that," Schofield told Fox News Digital. "Instead, Meghan’s first photographed social outing is with Ellen DeGeneres and Portia de Rossi. That tells me she remains very interested in celebrity and in being associated with recognizable, high-profile people." Schofield added that she finds it "interesting" that Markle "appears to have changed countries without necessarily changing the social ecosystem she prefers," noting that when living in Montecito, she and Prince Harry were spending time with "wealthy, famous and influential people." PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE ACCUSED OF SEEKING ‘BEST OF BOTH WORLDS’ WITH UK MOVE: EXPERT The idea that her first photographed outing since moving to the U.K. was with "two fellow American celebrity transplants" isn't "inherently wrong" in Schofield's eyes, but she argues that it challenges the "idea that Meghan has returned to Britain simply to embrace a quieter, more anonymous country life." "If anything, this suggests she may be trying to recreate elements of Montecito in the Cotswolds: privacy when she wants it, but with a glamorous and recognizable social circle around her," she said. MEGHAN MARKLE BEFORE ROYALTY: PHOTOS Prince Harry and Markle announced plans to return to the U.K. on Aug. 19 and relocated with their children later that month. British royals expert Hilary Fordwich agrees with Schofield, telling Fox News Digital that "Meghan Markle does nothing per chance" and was deliberately photographed with the celebrity couple to signal "for all to see that she’s extending her celebrity world from California to the Cotswolds, aiming to be viewed as significant." "She’s saying ‘I’m a Hollywood celebrity’ rather than a royal and am thus far 'sticking to celebrity lane insulated by privilege and not integrating into English life,'" Fordwich said. Schofield, however, questioned Markle's decision to have DeGeneres be the first celebrity she was photographed with, as "it inevitably resurrects an uncomfortable conversation for her." "Ellen’s reputation was badly damaged by allegations about the workplace culture surrounding her show, while Meghan herself has faced serious allegations about her treatment of Palace staff, which she has strongly denied," Schofield said. "Given that history, I am surprised Meghan would want photographs of the two of them together circulating so soon after her return to Britain. It invites comparisons I would imagine her advisers would rather avoid." articles.title: '80s star Tiffany steps into dream role after leaving Hollywood behind
articles.summary: Tiffany reveals her Off-Broadway role in "Spandex the Musical" fulfills a lifelong dream she put on hold when "I Think We're Alone Now" took off.
articles.body: '80s pop icon Tiffany is stepping back into the spotlight as she fulfills a dream she had prior to becoming a teen idol. The 54-year-old singer, who rose to fame in 1987 after her song "I Think We're Alone Now" became a massive hit, made her Off-Broadway debut in "Spandex the Musical" last week. During a July interview with People magazine, Tiffany reflected on why taking the stage felt like a "true full-circle moment for me." '80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD "Before music came into my life, I was a dancer and an actor, and those dreams were put on hold when ‘I Think We’re Alone Now’ took off and my recording career began," she said. Tiffany, whose full name is Tiffany Darwish, launched her career with the now-legendary Shopping Mall Tour '87, performing free concerts at malls across the country beginning in June 1987. The grassroots campaign helped turn the then-15-year-old into a teen sensation before she became a chart-topping artist. In September 1987, Tiffany's cover of Tommy James and the Shondells' 1967 hit "I Think We're Alone Now" climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 less than two months after its release and made her a household name. "I Think We're Alone Now" was the second single released from her self-titled debut album. She followed up with "Could've Been," the third single released from "Tiffany," which also topped the Billboard Hot 100. In addition, the album produced her Beatles cover "I Saw Him Standing There," which peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, and "Feelings of Forever," which reached the No. 50 spot. At 16, Tiffany became the youngest female artist to top the Billboard 200 with a debut album. She went on to headline her first major tour in 1988, with New Kids on the Block opening for her before the boy band's own meteoric rise. However, Tiffany's chart dominance proved difficult to sustain. While her 1988 sophomore album, "Hold an Old Friend's Hand," was certified platinum by the RIAA and produced the Top 10 hit "All This Time," it fell short of matching the success of her debut. As the teen-pop landscape shifted in the early 1990s, her third album, "New Inside," failed to gain commercial traction. RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD In 1993, Tiffany released her fourth album, "Dreams Never Die," which was issued only in Asian markets. She has also made appearances in movies and television shows and starred in several reality TV series. During a June interview with Fox News Digital, Tiffany detailed how she spent the past several years building a culinary brand that combines her love of cooking, entertaining and connecting with fans. articles.title: Wendi McLendon-Covey fires back after Jeff Garlin blames bipolar disorder for 'The Goldbergs' exit
articles.summary: Jeff Garlin says his undiagnosed bipolar disorder fueled the on-set behavior that led to his exit from "The Goldbergs." Co-star Wendi McLendon-Covey pushed back on his claims.
articles.body: Jeff Garlin is opening up about his contentious exit from "The Goldbergs," saying his undiagnosed bipolar disorder contributed to the behavior that strained relationships with his co-stars before he left the hit sitcom. The 64-year-old actor starred as the Goldbergs' family patriarch, Murray Goldberg, on the show from its premiere in September 2013 until he departed the ABC show during its ninth season in December 2021 amid HR investigations into complaints about his on-set behavior. Garlin was accused by members of the cast and crew of inappropriate verbal conduct, unwanted physical contact, including hugging and touching, and behavior that some employees described as creating an uncomfortable work environment. JEFF GARLIN DEFENDS HIMSELF FROM CANCEL CULTURE AMID ‘THE GOLDBERGS’ ON-SET CONDUCT ALLEGATIONS While speaking with Vanity Fair at the time, Garlin denied intentionally harassing anyone. He acknowledged that HR had spoken to him over several years but characterized the complaints as stemming from his style of comedy and "silliness" on set rather than malicious intent. He also said he was willing to adjust behaviors, like no longer hugging people. During a March 2023 appearance on SiriusXM's "Andy Cohen Live," Garlin's co-star, Wendi McLendon-Covey, who played his wife Beverly Goldberg on "The Goldbergs," said his exit was "a long time coming" and that "finally, someone is listening to us." She declined to discuss the situation further, saying she was "exhausted by that topic and the PTSD of it all." On Monday, Garlin appeared on the Daily Beast's "Obsessed" podcast and addressed McLendon-Covey's comments and attributed his behavior to a mental health condition that had not been diagnosed at the time. "It wasn't a long time coming for me," he said in reference to McLendon-Covey's past remark. "I actually empathize with her because, at the time, I was undiagnosed bipolar, and I was miserable on the show. "I was miserable with my performance," he continued. "She was always trying to tell me, 'Hey, you're really great on the show.' I didn't believe her, and I just got to the point where I had to quit. She was very resentful, and it was a bit dramatic. "I can only speak to what I'm responsible for," Garlin added. "Being bipolar, I was either one of three things: dark, dark, dark — where I didn't talk or look at anyone — happy to the point of mania, never turning off my thing or mean, really, really mean. I didn't know which one I was going to be. I didn't get diagnosed until I was 59. This was toward the end of my time on ‘The Goldbergs,’ so I could be a lot. 'BLUE BLOODS' STAR JENNIFER ESPOSITO SAYS SHE WAS LOCKED IN PSYCH WARD AS HEALTH BATTLE SPIRALED "When I left, she was very resentful and angry at me. If she wants to continue the resentment, that's her. I don't have resentment toward her, even for saying things about me. I actually love her, and I appreciate that she's one of the greatest actors I've ever worked with. And that will not be lost on me." McLendon-Covey, 56, responded to Garlin's comments after the Daily Beast shared a clip from his interview on Instagram. "Huh," she wrote in the comments section. After an Instagram user asked her, "What’s your take, Wendi?," the "Bridesmaids" star wrote, "Let's just say I remember things very differently, as does the crew, the other actors, the writers and our executives." Fox News Digital has reached out to representatives for Garlin and McLendon-Covey for comment. "The Goldbergs" followed the misadventures of a loud but loving family living in suburban Philadelphia during the 1980s. Though Garlin left "The Goldbergs" during its ninth season, he was a regular cast member for part of that season. After his exit, the show completed some remaining Season 9 episodes using previously filmed footage and stand-ins before writing Murray Goldberg out ahead of Season 10. At the beginning of the tenth season, the show revealed that the character had died off-screen, allowing the series to continue focusing on the Goldberg family without him. ABC announced in February 2023 that Season 10 would be the show's last, and the series finale aired on May 3, 2023. articles.title: Jay-Z accuser says her rape claims against him were false
articles.summary: The woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has recanted her allegations against the music mogul.
articles.body: The woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has recanted her allegations against the music mogul. In a filing Thursday from lawyers representing Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, the former accuser says that her allegations against the rapper were “false,” adding that she “never met Mr. Carter. Mr. Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever. There is no truth to any of my claims against Mr. Carter.” In the filing, she added that she falsely claimed that Carter and Sean “Diddy” Combs raped her while watched by another celebrity, whose name is redacted. The filing is part of Carter’s ongoing malicious prosecution lawsuit against the woman’s former attorney, Tony Buzbee, which was filed in February 2025 in New York. Carter’s lawyers said this week they were dropping the woman, known as Jane Doe, from the suit. Buzbee, Jane Doe, and representatives for Carter and Combs didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. Combs is serving a sentence in federal prison after he was convicted in July 2025 of prostitution-related crimes, in a separate case. The woman came forward in December 2024, in a civil lawsuit filed by Buzbee, accusing Carter and Combs of raping her at a house party following the 2000 MTV Video Music Awards, which were held in New York. Days after the suit was filed, she sat down with NBC News for an interview and doubled down on her claims. But after NBC News pointed out inconsistencies in her account, she said in a subsequent phone interview that she had “made some mistakes.” At the time, Combs’ attorneys described the suit as a “shameful money grab” while Carter’s lawyer Alex Spiro called it a “frivolous case.” In February 2025, Jane Doe dropped her lawsuit with prejudice, meaning she couldn’t file it again. In this week’s filing, Jane Doe writes: “I understand that my false accusations have caused Mr. Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone. I sincerely and unconditionally apologize to Mr. Carter for the devastating harm I have caused to him, his family and his reputation.” She also says in the filing that Buzbee and his team paid her $1,000 before sitting down for NBC News’ interview. In a separate suit, Jay-Z initially sued Buzbee in 2024 in California, accusing Buzbee of extortion and defamation. It was dismissed in June 2025, and the California Court of Appeals affirmed that decision earlier this month. Representatives for Buzbee and his law firm called the appeals court’s ruling “a complete vindication for our clients.”

articles.title: Even as a new ‘Great British Bake Off’ judge, Nigella Lawson can’t escape the memes
articles.summary: “Great British Bake Off” fans were excited about Nigella Lawson’s debut on season 17 of the baking competition show. But many also poked fun at her mannerisms.
articles.body: Years after mispronouncing “microwave” on BBC’s “Cook, Eat, Repeat,” food writer Nigella Lawson has found herself at the center of yet another viral frenzy. This time, the response has largely come from fans of the popular competition show “The Great British Bake Off,” who are poking fun at Lawson for a different on-air quirk: How she bites into baked goods. “The Great British Baking Show,” which is known as “The Great British Bake Off” (or GBBO) overseas, first launched in 2010 on the BBC. It has since exploded into a beloved, global phenomenon with a fervent fan base. Lawson replaced Prue Leith as a judge on season 17 of the baking show, which aired Tuesday in the U.K. and will premiere Friday in the U.S. on Netflix. Longtime viewers were saddened by Leith’s decision to exit the series, even though the 86-year-old said in her announcement that it “feels like the right time to step back.” Overall, Lawson’s debut has been well received. But many fans were quick to point out a mannerism they just couldn’t get past. “Apparently Nigella Lawson is capable of unhinging her jaw to swallow her prey,” one user wrote on X, alongside a photo of her taking a bite of a cake. Another said: “I can’t stop laughing at the way Nigella eats these cakes like she’s eating as if she’s never eaten before.” Some posts included harsher jabs, such as describing Lawson’s eating as “really weird,” though not all the content was mean spirited. Several parody videos of people shoveling dessert into their mouths also circulated on social media. Still, Lawson’s bigger bites didn’t hinder overall enthusiasm for her presence on the show. Critics have praised Lawson’s culinary expertise, and many fans online have described her as a “perfect” addition. Giuseppe Dell’Anno, a former “Bake Off” winner, told BBC Radio 4’s Today that Lawson is a “nice fit with the ethos of the program.” Her arrival in the white tent was also welcomed by longtime judge Paul Hollywood. “It was lovely to see Nigella come into the tent,” he told The Guardian last week. “She fitted in beautifully — not just with me but with the whole team. She picked up the ‘Bake Off’ vibe straight away.” And as for Lawson herself? Enjoyment is all part of the “Bake Off” experience. “I don’t have many skills,” she joked in the first episode, “but eating is one of them.”
